Sports.title: F1 Dutch GP red-flagged after Verstappen crash
Sports.content:
Formula 1's Dutch Grand Prix has been red-flagged after one lap following an enormous accident for home hero Max Verstappen.

At the end of lap 1 on a damp circuit, Verstappen lost control of his Red Bull as he tagged the white line on the inside of Zandvoort's final turn - the banked, flat out Luyendyk corner leading onto the main straight.

Verstappen veered head on into the outside wall, before his car crossed the track and came to a standstill on the inside.

The Dutchman soon reported he was OK and apologised to his team for ending his race early.

Verstappen was fortunate not to be collected by any other cars, with Alpine's Pierre Gasly taking avoiding action, while in the background Audi's Nico Hulkenberg also narrowly avoided a huge accident as his team-mate Gabriel Bortoleto spun in front of him.

Under the red flag all drivers gathered in the pitlane awaiting the restart. They were having to navigate a field of debris before pit entry, but teams are allowed to change tyres under a red flag ahead of the restart. That restart is expected at 15:33 local time.

Max Verstappen Photo by: Anni Graf - Formula 1 via Getty Images

At the time Verstappen was running seventh after a disappointing qualifying session. Polesitter Lando Norris retained his lead during a chaotic start sequence, with championship leader Kimi Antonelli passing George Russell for second.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc gaining two positions to hold down fourth ahead of the second McLaren of Oscar Piastri and team-mate Lewis Hamilton.

For Verstappen, the accident marks an unfortunate end to a six-year spell racing on home soil, winning the first three editions of the Dutch Grand prix revival in 2021, 2022 and 2023. The race will disappear from the calendar after organisers decided not to pursue a contract renewal with F1 management.

Earlier in the week, the four-time world champion announced he had extended his Red Bull contract until the end of the 2030 season.

Sports.title: Wolff jokes that Mercedes already has Verstappen for the "real hero races"
Sports.content:
As is tradition, Mercedes organises a special media session with Wolff and representatives of the Dutch press at Zandvoort. In recent years, those roundtables have often produced some eye-catching comments, much to the amusement of Mercedes team members as well.

Two years ago at Zandvoort, for example, Wolff more or less confirmed Kimi Antonelli's F1 promotion, even though the formal announcement was not scheduled until a week later at Monza.

Last year, Wolff spoke openly about the talks with Verstappen over a potential move to Mercedes and caused some surprise when the subject turned to several AI-generated pictures of the pair. Wolff also joked about AI-generated images of himself and Verstappen, including explicit deepfakes circulating online.

At the start of this year’s conversation, Wolff clearly still remembered all those moments and laughed: “You know, let me get into the groove and then I'll give you a few punchlines!”

Dacia, Verstappen and "hero races" at the Nordschleife

#3 Mercedes-AMG Team Verstappen Racing, Mercedes AMG GT3 EVO: Max Verstappen, Daniel Juncadella, Jules Gounon, Lucas Auer Photo by: Red Bull Content Pool

Wolff then addressed Verstappen’s new Red Bull deal. According to the Mercedes team principal, the chances of a move were greater last year than they have been over the past few months, something that already became clear in the spring.

During last year’s Dutch media session, Wolff said he felt their paths would cross at some point. Asked by Autosport whether Verstappen’s new Red Bull contract has definitively changed that feeling, Wolff clarified that, in his view, their paths are already crossing – just not in F1.

“Well, the paths have crossed already with the GT racing. I think when we jointly developed that programme a year and a half ago it seemed a long shot,” Wolff said. “It seemed to be a long shot because could Red Bull ever allow Max in a Mercedes GT3?

“But they were open-minded and we are thankful for that because the project has been a success, the Red Bull Mercedes project. We have this joint cooperation between the two brands and Max, and it is nice to see that it’s successful.”

#3 Mercedes-AMG Team Verstappen Racing, Mercedes AMG GT3 EVO: Max Verstappen, Daniel Juncadella, Jules Gounon, Lucas Auer Photo by: Qian Jun / MB Media / Getty Images

Wolff then joked that Mercedes therefore gets Verstappen for what he considers the “real hero races” — the endurance events on the Nordschleife, with the Nurburgring 24 Hours as the absolute highlight.

“Exactly! You know, we have these things here in F1 with massive gravel traps and flat run-off zones. The real racing is where you go through the trees and up and downs over crests and blind corners. And against the Dacia!”

With those final words, Wolff is referring to Olli’s Garage Racing, which competes with a Dacia Logan in the iconic 24-hour race in the Green Hell.

After mentioning the Dacia, Wolff immediately turned to the press officer present, telling him that Mercedes should invite the Dacia crew to an actual F1 Grand Prix.

“No, seriously, they are heroes!” Wolff laughed. All of those things contribute to the magic of the Nordschleife, with Wolff enjoying seeing Verstappen behind the wheel of the Winward Mercedes-AMG GT3.

“You race against 150 cars on the Nordschleife in day and night, fog and rain, and ice. So obviously none of these races are 24 hours, but those are the real hero races.”

Could Verstappen ever get the same freedom at Mercedes?

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Mark Thompson / Getty Images

Whether Verstappen and Wolff’s paths will ever cross in F1 is something the latter does not dare to predict, if only because nobody knows what the driver market will look like in two or three years’ time.

“And what the future holds, I don't know, but the mindset is what I have just said. I don't know where the paths are going to cross. Will it be in karting, will it be in GTs, or will it be in F1 or some other joint projects in the future?

“I think that may happen one day, but maybe not necessarily with Max in a Mercedes Formula 1 car.”

The latter may not be necessary either, now that Mercedes already has its star of the future in Kimi Antonelli.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes Photo by: Andy Hone/ LAT Images via Getty Images

Another question is whether Verstappen would receive the same freedom to pursue outside racing projects at another F1 team.

“I think every team is different, but I think what I am trying to do is to identify what it is that makes the driver fast within our structure.

“What kind of framework do we need to provide to extract the best performance of the driver, and part of that is obviously the well-being. And that is something that I am very keen on as well.”

Sports.title: Verstappen suffering from "flu-like" illness as Zandvoort exposes Red Bull's fundamental problems
Sports.content:
With three victories since the Dutch Grand Prix returned to the calendar in 2021, Max Verstappen can already look back on a very successful period. The final edition in 2026 has proven an ordeal so far, both in terms of Red Bull’s pace and Verstappen’s physical condition.

"I've felt better before, yes," Verstappen admitted during the Dutch media session in the paddock after qualifying. "I feel a bit flu-like and I’m just not feeling as much energy as normal."

Asked whether that also affects his performance behind the wheel, he continued: "No, I don’t think so. I think once you’re in the car, it’s actually fine."

It does mean Verstappen is experiencing his final home race somewhat differently and is mainly looking forward to the moment he can get some rest: "Of course I still enjoy all the fans in the grandstands, but apart from that, I’m mostly looking forward to getting some sleep."

Why Zandvoort exposes some fundamental Red Bull problems

Aside from Verstappen’s physical condition, Red Bull is also struggling for performance at the circuit in the dunes. The home hero had to settle for seventh on the grid and was more than four tenths behind polesitter Lando Norris in qualifying.

"We changed quite a lot on the car after the sprint, but none of it made any difference," Verstappen said when asked by Autosport.

According to Verstappen, the Zandvoort circuit exposes some of Red Bull’s weaknesses to an exaggerated degree Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

"The balance of the car is the biggest problem. It’s just not consistent throughout the entire corner, but it has been like that all season. It’s just a little worse at some circuits than at others."

In that respect, Zandvoort is a track that exposes the RB22’s weaknesses more than most.

"It depends on the tarmac sometimes, but also on the layout of the track. This one is for sure not our best layout, but we just need to work on it. We can guess on what track it might be a little bit better, but we need to try and just dial it out."

Verstappen added that, in his view, it is not so much related to set-up, as Red Bull has tried everything in that respect: "I think we’re now simply more limited by some fundamental problems with the car that we need to solve.

"At this circuit you also have some fast corners and we’re lacking there as well. In general, if you don’t have a good balance, you can’t really attack the corners. And if you don’t have traction either, you can’t get out of the corners properly, so all of that costs time."

It means Verstappen considers seventh place the maximum achievable result on Sunday under normal circumstances, particularly if there is no chaos caused by rain.

Without rain, Verstappen reckons that P7 will be the best he can hope for in his final home race Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

It may not be the Zandvoort farewell he had hoped for, although the four-time world champion stresses that the Dutch GP era as a whole has already been a great success.

"It’s absolutely the end of an era," he said. "To have had your own home race and to have been able to win it a few times is very special. Of course, it’s a shame that it’s going away, but on the other hand, it has also given me a lot of great moments and memories."

Whether another memorable moment will be added remains to be seen, but Verstappen took a pragmatic view in conclusion.

"I’m really only satisfied when we win, but that’s going to be very difficult tomorrow," he said. "We’ve been a little too slow throughout this season and that’s not suddenly going to change in Zandvoort, but we’re just going to try to enjoy it one last time."

Sports.title: Russell defends “fair” decision to let Antonelli into second place | Formula 1
Sports.content:
George Russell said letting his team mate and championship rival overtake him was the correct decision which minimised the risk to their races.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli ran ahead of Russell until he made an extra pit stop during a late Virtual Safety Car period. When Antonelli closed on Russell afterwards, Mercedes ordered the pair to swap positions.

Russell complied, though it handed Antonelli a six-point swing in the championship fight between the pair of them. That erased the gain Russell made in the previous day’s sprint race.

However Russell said letting his team mate by was the correct thing to do for Mercedes.

“We’ve always said as a team, when we’re on different strategies, we’re never going to fight and we’re always going to invert, and that’s always just been our rules,” he explained.

“The fact is Kimi was ahead of me before the VSC and he tried something different to protect us as a team. He kind of copy-pasted what the Ferraris did.”

Although Russell believes there was a chance he could have successfully defended his position from Antonelli – as he later did with Lewis Hamilton, thanks partly to the timing of another VSC period – he also said trying to defend could have compromised his race.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“Could I have kept him behind? Maybe. But equally it could have been a P5 as well. So, in the end, you know, he deserved to be P2. I think P3 was a fair result for me.”

Russell fell behind Antonelli at the start of the race, then got stuck behind Oscar Piastri and never managed to get back on terms with his team mate. “It was tough,” he said.

“The first VSC came at a pretty awkward timing for me because I felt really strong on the hard [tyre]. I think Kimi’s and my race was kind of the opposite. I had a tough medium stint, he had a very strong medium stint, then I had a strong hard stint, he was struggling.

“But that VSC gave Lewis a free pit stop and obviously Kimi pitted as well. And from there on in, I knew I was going to be under threat.

“I was managing enough in the high-speed corners to allow me to be fast in sector three and defending into turn one [Tarzan]. So I was pleased with that performance.”

Sports.title: Antonelli says extra pit stop “put George at risk” too | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli was not convinced his extra pit stop in the Dutch Grand Prix was the right decision as it risked compromising his race.

The Mercedes driver made an extra pit stop 16 laps from the end of the race, taking advantage of a late Virtual Safety Car period. It dropped him from second place to third behind his team mate George Russell

Antonelli was able to repass his team mate for second place after Mercedes ordered Russell to let him through. However Antonelli was unable to gain on race leader Lando Norris.

Afterwards Antonelli said the strategy call had unnecessarily risked both their races, even though he had been struggling on his previous set of tyres.

“It was a difficult second half for me, especially in the last stint on the hards,” he said. “I was just really struggling. I had little confidence in the car and it was not easy.

“Then obviously we pitted [under the VSC] and also that was a bit tricky. But then also George, I have to thank him because he made my life a lot easier.

“But I still think probably we could have stayed out and gone until the end with the same set [of tyres] because it put us a little bit at risk. Also, I feel we put George at risk with having to let me by and everything.”

Although he led most of the race, Antonelli said he was unlikely to win it. “I still think, at the end of the day, it was a great team execution with how things were,” he said. “”I think today [second place] was the maximum we could have done because the pace of the McLarens, especially in the second half, was just too strong.”

“It was a good ending of a difficult weekend for me where I struggled with the feeling of the car, did a lot of mistakes on my side – sprint quali, quali, also in today’s race with Lando I could have defended a bit better,” he added. “So for sure there were things that I didn’t do well this weekend, and for sure the feeling wasn’t as good.”

Sports.title: “We weren’t unlucky”: Hamilton tells Ferrari their tactics cost him third place | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton told Ferrari they cost him a chance to finish third by failing to use team orders during the Dutch Grand Prix.

He finished fourth behind George Russell after losing time earlier in the race when he caught team mate Charles Leclerc. Hamilton repeatedly urged Ferrari to tell Leclerc to let him through, but the team instead to chose wait a lap and then bring the leading Ferrari into the pits.

“Let’s not hold ourselves up from an potentially better result,” Hamilton told the team when he caught Leclerc.

After spending a lap behind Leclerc, Hamilton warned Ferrari “we’re just losing time.” Once Leclerc came in, Hamilton sarcastically remarked: “Big waste of time guys, good job.”

Hamilton’s attempt to pass Russell at the end of the race was thwarted when the Virtual Safety Car was deployed. After he finished fourth race engineer Carlos Santi told Hamilton: “Thank you Lewis, was a bit unlucky with Russell.”

“We weren’t unlucky,” Hamilton replied, “we lost time earlier on and that cost us P3.”

“We can discuss it offline,” he added.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Hamilton explained his frustration after the race, pointing out Mercedes did not hesitate to swap the order of their two drivers when it benefitted them overall.

“I want to win,” said Hamilton. “I’m here to win and it is difficult when you’re looking ahead and you see the two Mercedes drivers, they get the call and it’s done and they execute straight away.

“They let Kimi by and let him get on with the race. I was on a different strategy and it was not the same here.

“That’s a little bit difficult but we just have to take it, we’ll take it off line. When I go back now, I’ll speak to them about it.”

Sports.title: Williams pair apologise for crash: ‘It’s not a Verstappen-Ricciardo Baku situation’ | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Both Williams drivers apologised for their roles in the collision between the pair during the Dutch Grand Prix.

However the stewards ruled Carlos Sainz Jnr was responsible for the collision which ended his team mate Alexander Albon’s race.

The collision occured as Albon tried to overtake Sainz on the outside entering Tarzan corner. Sainz locked up and made contact with the other Williams.

“It was a situation of the race put us with Alex on a fresher medium [tyre] behind,” Sainz explained. “I was struggling already a lot with my hard tyres there towards the end of the race and all of a sudden when I went to defend, a big bump in the braking area into turn one surprised me.

“I triggered a massive front lock and without wanting, obviously, I took Alex with me, which is the last thing you want to do with a team mate. But honestly I was caught off guard with that big bump there in the braking and triggered a massive front lock that I couldn’t recover later.

“So apologies for that and we will move on as a team. I think it’s just not the position we want to be in.”

The stewards handed Sainz a 10-second time penalty, ruling he “locked up and caused a collision between both cars” and was “wholly at fault”.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

However Albon also apologised for his role in the collision. He said it was not as serious as other clashes between team mates, notably the 2018 collision between Red Bull duo Max Verstappen and Daniel Ricciardo at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix which took both drivers out.

“It’s not good for the team,” said Albon. “Obviously we apologise to the team, but it’s not a Verstappen-Ricciardo Baku situation.

“We’ll review it for sure but I think he maybe just locked up and I tried to avoid it as well but we had damage so we had to retire.”

Sports.title: Hulkenberg explains how he avoided team mate Bortoleto in “scary” near-miss | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Nico Hulkenberg described how he made an “instinctive” last-second swerve to avoid T-boning his team mate in the Dutch Grand Prix.

Gabriel Bortoleto overtook Hulkenberg moments before spinning in front of him on the first lap of the Dutch Grand Prix.

“It was scary, sketchy,” said Hulkenberg. “You’re a passenger to some [extent].”

Bortoleto lost control of his car in the final corner, moments after Max Verstappen did the same and hit the barrier on the outside. Bortoleto kept his car on track but Hulkenberg had to make an immediate call whether to swerve to the left or right of the other Audi.

“I tried to react as late as possible and then just instinctively chose the side,” Hulkenberg explained. “Obviously I was waiting to see if he’s going to slide up or down. On a wet track it’s sketchy and difficult, but luckily we managed to avoid that.”

Bortoleto suspected he lost control of his car partly because he saw Verstappen going off ahead of him.

“I just saw big smoke coming out,” he said. “I think it was Max that crashed and then I maybe made a small reaction on the steering.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“But I just felt something and then I also lost the car. I did a 360, came back.”

Both Audi drivers finished the race, Hulkenberg claiming points for eighth while Bortoleto’s poor start and spin left him 13th. Bortoleto said he had other “issues” in his race but was unwilling to elaborate on them.

“I don’t want to go too much into details, because I don’t know if I can say, or whatever. But we just need to understand some stuff that happened today, and we’ll move on.

“I had a few start problems today that almost made me not probably manage to run out of the grid box, but I appreciate the work of the team. They were really on it to make it happen and to fix everything.

“It’s a shame the result was not what we wanted today, but Nico scored some points, so that’s good. We brought some points for the team at home, so good.”

Sports.title: Colapinto claims penalty for overtaking under yellow flags was “very harsh” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Franco Colapinto committed two yellow flag infringements during the Dutch Grand Prix and was given penalty points on his licence for each.

Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad were also penalised for failing to obey F1’s yellow flag rules.

Colapinto’s first penalty was for overtaking Yuki Tsunoda as they passed double waved yellow flags on the first lap of the race. The flags were shown in response to Max Verstappen’s crash at the final corner, which littered the track with debris, as well as Gabriel Bortoleto’s 360-degree spin at the same corner.

“Car 43 [Colapinto] was behind car 22 [Tsunoda] entering turn 14 and overtook car 22 in the double yellow flag sector before the [finishing] line at the end of lap one,” the stewards noted.

“Normally such infringement requires a 10 second stop[-and-]go penalty, but the stewards acknowledge the complications caused by the significant amount of debris on track at this point and take this into account as mitigating circumstances.”

The stewards issued the same decision regarding Arvid Lindblad who overtook Pierre Gasly at the same time. Both Colapinto and Lindblad received drive-through penalties and two penalty points on their licences.

Colapinto was already gaining on Tsunoda as they rounded the final corner when Verstappen crashed ahead of them. He continued to pass the Racing Bulls as the crash unfolded ahead of them.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

The Alpine driver criticised the stewards’ decision, calling it a “very harsh penalty” which “Colapinto: compromised the whole of our race”.

“It’s quite tricky, I think, to manage those situations when there is a car and pieces of car everywhere flying around and you have to make a decision,” he explained. “It was clearly much more dangerous to slam on the brakes in the middle of the straight and on the water and on the banking and not doing what I’ve done.

“I guess the rules are written [this way] but it should be much more flexible and give a little bit more, not just consistency, but a bit of flexibility in different situations that you can clearly see that this shouldn’t be penalised exactly what the rules say. But in the end of the day we still lead an infringement.”

Colapinto received another penalty point, and a 10-second time penalty, for failing to slow sufficiently for yellow flags later in the race when Esteban Ocon retired. The stewards noted he “passed a single yellow flag without discernibly reducing speed although also

receiving a visible warning on the dash.”

“As the infringement was not considered dangerous or egregious, a penalty on the lower end of the available scale is imposed,” they added. They also found Liam Lawson guilty of the same infraction and issued the same penalty.

The decisions leave Colapinto on a total of four penalty points, Lawson on three and Lindblad on two.

Sports.title: Teofimo Defeats Rolly, Now He Has His Eyes Set On Undisputed
Sports.content:
During the first three rounds of the world title bout, Lopez was in control as he used his jab and touched the body of Romero. Late in the fourth round, Romero landed a check left hook that knocked Lopez off balance.

In the fifth round, Rolly got more aggressive, and as a result, he landed a big left hook that produced a cut over Teofimo’s right eye.

Seconds later, Romero connected with a vicious overhand right that buckled Lopez’s knees.

Romero followed the big right hand with a flurry of shots, but Lopez was able to survive the round. Lopez bounced back in the sixth as he returned to his game plan of working off the jab and attacking the body.

Lopez continued to apply intelligent pressure in the seventh as he landed a solid right hand. As round seven was coming to a close, Romero caught Lopez with a powerful check left hook.

For the remainder of the WBA welterweight title bout, Teofimo Lopez fought a smart and very disciplined fight. Despite the low punch output, Rolly had the more eye-catching shots, but Teofimo outworked him and won by majority decision.

With the victory, Teofimo “The Takeover” Lopez (23-2, 13 KOs) became a three-division world champion. As soon as Lopez was announced as the winner, the boxing community was seeking the answer to the proverbial question: What’s next?

During the post-fight press conference, Teofimo Lopez spoke about his future and the path he plans to travel in his boxing journey.

“I think I’m here, this is the road to undisputed, you know what I’m saying? I’m here to reclaim and collect all of the next world titles, and whoever the next champion is, that’s what it’s all about.”

Teofimo Lopez went on to say, “Honestly, I got four fights with, well now three fights with DAZN, and all of them are the road to undisputed. We’re going right to every world title.”

Currently, the world champions in the welterweight division are Teofimo Lopez (WBA), Devin Haney (WBO), Ryan Garcia (WBC), and Liam Paro (IBF). In his quest to become undisputed, the first step for Lopez is to become a unified world champion.

If Lopez wants what looks like the softer touch, a unification bout with IBF champion Liam Paro may be next. If Lopez wants a fight that is going to be a big event, then he may want to pursue a bout with the Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn winner.

Sports.title: Moises Garcia Derails Mike Tyson Look-Alike’s Hype Train
Sports.content:
Coming into the bout, D’Angelo Evans was the featured attraction due to his look, his KO percentage, and his most recent knockout that went viral. Most fight fans didn’t know D’Angelo Evans existed until his viral moment.

Back in May 2026, with 2:05 remaining in the second round, D’Angelo “Muscle” Evans landed a vicious left hook that knocked Cesar Villarraga out cold. The match came to an abrupt end as Villarraga was immediately attended to.

Once the knockout video hit the internet, casual fans started comparing Evans to a young Mike Tyson because of his facial features and his KO power. Some casuals went as far as making fake videos claiming Evans is Mike Tyson’s son.

Going into his August 22nd bout, the people who jumped on the D’Angelo Evans hype train were expecting another viral moment. Unfortunately, they witnessed a moment that no one predicted.

Prior to the August 22nd bout, Moises Garcia lost two fights in a row. Garcia went back to the drawing board, and he bounced back by putting together a two-fight win streak.

In his April 2026 fight, Garcia lost by way of unanimous decision to Top Rank’s rising undefeated prospect Deric “Scooter” Davis. Four months later, Garcia was scheduled to fight another prospect who was rapidly gaining momentum.

On the night of August 22nd, with 1:47 remaining in the 5th round, Garcia landed a hard left hook that staggered Evans. D’Angelo Evans showed his inexperience by retreating straight backward rather than clinching or angling out.

Garcia pressed forward and landed a flurry of shots that produced a knockdown. D’Angelo Evans was unable to get up, and just like that, the hype train got derailed.

With the victory, the Puebla, Puebla, Mexico native Moises “Bam-Bam” Garcia improved to a record of (8-6-3, 4 KOs). Now the question is, will the big promotional companies take a chance on matching their rising prospects against the upset-minded Garcia?

For D’Angelo Evans, it’s time to regroup. From an offensive standpoint, Evans has some tools, but to bounce back effectively, he must work on his defense and learn to fight off the back foot.

Sports.title: Joe Joyce Wants Return Despite Suslenkov Memory Blank
Sports.content:
“I went back to the hotel room, and I was like, ‘What really happened?’ I felt like I was winning the fight, and then I watched it back, and I was like, ‘Whoa.’ I think what might have happened, I might have taken a big shot. I couldn’t really see,” said Joyce to talkSPORT Boxing.

Joyce is currently without a promoter and floated Dana White’s Zuffa Boxing as one possible destination. He did not claim that White had contacted him or made an offer.

“Zuffa would be—I’d be open to having a conversation with Dana White. Have a conversation with everyone, see what’s out there.”

Five of Joyce’s last six contests have ended in defeat. The decline began against Zhilei Zhang in April 2023, when repeated left hands damaged his right eye and forced a sixth-round stoppage. Zhang then knocked him out in three rounds in their rematch five months later.

Losses to Filip Hrgovic, Derek Chisora, and Suslenkov followed. The Chisora and Suslenkov defeats were especially revealing. Neither man performed like a top heavyweight. They were simply able to outwork and punish a version of Joyce who no longer resembled the fighter who stopped Joseph Parker in 2022.

His weight has not helped. Joyce was 256 pounds for the first Zhang fight after spending much of his earlier career in the 250s and low 260s. He rose to 281¼ for the rematch, 286½ against Kash Ali, 281¼ for Chisora, and a career-high 289 against Suslenkov.

Joyce was never quick, but carrying nearly 290 pounds has made him look even slower. His punches are painfully slow, his feet are heavier, and opponents have more time to land shots. Only Joyce knows why he has not returned to a lower weight. The way he looks now, he’s puffy and looks nothing like he did when he turned pro in 2017.

Trainer SugarHill Steward supported his decision to stop against Suslenkov after noticing signs of fatigue. Steward believes regular gym work can bring back some of the athletic ability missing from Joyce’s recent performances.

That is difficult to accept after watching his decline over the last three years. Joyce built his career around absorbing punishment and wearing opponents down, but his resistance is no longer reliable. Forgetting how the Suslenkov fight finished makes another return even more concerning.

Joyce named Daniel Dubois, Joseph Parker, Hrgovic, and Chisora as possible rematch opponents. That is a tough list for someone with one win since September 2022. At 40, with his durability fading and weight continuing to rise, there is little reason to believe he will become the fighter he was before Zhang. If Joyce remains in the 280s, more defeats are likely.

Sports.title: Putting Moses Itauma Behind A Paywall Hurts His Future
Sports.content:
Fans are being asked to pay to watch an unproven 21-year-old headline against an opponent who is respected within boxing but has little drawing power. A bare-bones undercard filled with domestic-level scrubs going nowhere gives undecided buyers zero reason to order the event.

Thin Card Leaves Itauma Carrying The Show

Sam Noakes against former WBO lightweight champion Denys Berinchyk is the strongest supporting fight. Constantin Ursu meets Ben Vaughan, Aloys Junior takes on 40-year-old Mike Perez, and Guido Vianello faces Moses Jolly.

Those fights may serve their purpose on a regular DAZN card, but this is a premium broadcast. None carries enough public interest to take pressure off Itauma and Hrgovic.

The promoters are trying to collect star-level money before Itauma has become a star. That strategy reduces the number of people who will see him and makes it harder for him to develop the support required to sell future events.

Exposure Should Come Before PPV

Regular cards should remain Itauma’s home until he is at least 26 and has been shown repeatedly to boxing fans. Five more years of accessible fights would let viewers follow his development, learn his personality, and become invested in his career.

Anthony Joshua became a major attraction because millions of British viewers watched his early fights. Itauma is being denied that broad introduction by a business model that demands payment without first establishing a connection with the public.

An IBF title would give Itauma a belt, but it would not automatically make him an attraction. Hiding him behind a paywall may bring in money on August 29. It also means fewer people will be watching when he takes the most important step of his career.

Sports.title: Hearn Claims TKO Paid For Tyson Fury Story Reposts
Sports.content:
“Firstly, that’s a plant,” Hearn said after revealing that BoxingScene reporter Lance Pugmire had contacted him about an email he received. “It was sent by TKO to journalists. I actually was told by a number of people that they’re financially incentivizing people to repost Tyson Fury’s story of him trying to spin the narrative. It’s absolutely wild what’s going on.”

Hearn then disputed how the circulated document had been presented.

“The email that was sent was an email between Matchroom and Sela detailing outstanding points that we want resolved. The addendum that was sent to Sela regarding the changes that we want to the contract if you want to do the fight in the US did not have one of those things from that leaked email in.”

Selective Leak or Paid Campaign?

At least two media outlets obtained the disputed information. Hearn named Pugmire, while The Sun stated that it was among several media organizations given the material. No complete list of recipients has been made public.

That reinforces Hearn’s contention that the email was circulated selectively, though it falls well short of proving that reporters received financial incentives. Providing favorable information to selected reporters is a familiar tactic during a contentious negotiation. Pugmire’s possession of the material only shows that someone wanted its contents made public. It does not reveal who sent it directly or establish that money changed hands.

The distinction between the email and the addendum is also central to Hearn’s defense. He maintains that the leaked correspondence covered unresolved business between Matchroom and Sela, while the addendum contained separate terms required for moving Joshua vs Fury from Britain to the United States.

Until Hearn produces evidence, the alleged paid media campaign remains hearsay. Obtaining a leaked document is not proof that a reporter was rewarded for publicizing it.

Sports.title: Julian Jackson vs Gerald McClellan: Five Rounds of Violence
Sports.content:
Seven years younger, McClellan arrived from Emanuel Steward’s Kronk Gym with a 27-2 record and 26 knockouts. The challenger attacked with the speed, aggression, and confidence of a fighter who did not expect his opponents to survive long.

This was more than a meeting of knockout artists. Jackson had to prove that his experience and single-punch power remained enough to stop a younger destroyer. McClellan needed to show that his quick victories had prepared him for a champion who punched harder than anyone he had faced.

Jackson Tests McClellan’s Chin

McClellan struck first, hurting Jackson with a right hand during the opening round. The champion recovered and began landing hard punches to the body in the second. A heavy left hook downstairs hurt McClellan and forced him to retreat. Jackson kept attacking the body in the third, using feints to slow the challenger’s aggression and create openings for his wider punches.

An accidental clash of heads left Jackson bleeding and resulted in a point deduction from McClellan under WBC rules. Jackson already had a history of eye trouble, making the damage especially concerning.

After four rounds, two judges had Jackson leading 38-37, while the third had the fight even at 38-38.

Low Blows Trigger a Brutal Finish

Two low punches from Jackson interrupted the fifth. McClellan went down after the second and received time to recover, giving the champion a brief pause after several physically punishing rounds.

The break had the opposite effect. Once Mills Lane restarted the fight, McClellan drove a right hand into Jackson’s head and followed with left hooks that sent the champion onto his back. Jackson somehow rose, but his bloody face and unstable legs showed how badly he had been shaken. Another attack dropped him a second time. Lane stopped the fight at 2:09 without allowing Jackson another chance to continue.

The stoppage earned The Ring magazine’s 1993 Knockout of the Year award. McClellan won their rematch by first-round knockout one year later, but the original fight remains the more revealing contest.

Jackson showed that McClellan could be hurt, yet hurting him was not enough. After recovering from the low blow, the challenger turned a close middleweight fight into a violent ending within seconds.

Sports.title: Xander Zayas Faces Dangerous Road At Middleweight
Sports.content:
That is an ambitious schedule for a 23-year-old coming off a seventh-round stoppage. Ennis dropped Zayas three times and took control once he began applying steady pressure. The additional six pounds will not erase what happened or give Zayas the punching power needed to hold off natural middleweights.

Power was never one of his strengths at junior middleweight. He scored 13 knockouts in his first 23 victories, often relying on combinations and movement rather than ending fights with one shot. His punches may carry even less authority against opponents accustomed to taking shots from 160-pound fighters.

Careful matchmaking will be necessary if Top Rank intends to get Zayas into a championship fight before the end of 2027. Yoenli Hernandez would be an especially difficult opponent because of his size, activity and strength.

None of the current champions offers an easy opening. Carlos Adames brings the pressure and power that gave Zayas trouble against Ennis. Aaron McKenna is physically strong and willing to fight at a high pace. Erislandy Lara remains a skilled counterpuncher despite his age, while Denzel Bentley has enough size and power to punish mistakes.

A ranked opponent who allows Zayas to settle into the new division can be found for February. Getting him from that bout to a title opportunity without crossing one of the division’s most dangerous fighters will be the difficult part.

He may feel better at 160, but comfort alone will not make him stronger, more durable, or harder to pressure. His middleweight campaign will depend as much on opponent selection as improvement.

Sports.title: Jack Catterall Blocks Teofimo Lopez’s Three-Unification Plan
Sports.content:
“180 days @WBABoxing which means November ✅ I understand the politics of boxing better than most. Rolly had a voluntary; now it’s time for my shot! No ducks, no more swerving. Me v Teo next,” said Catterall on X.

His message also answered Teofimo’s intention to pursue three consecutive unification matches without making a mandatory defense. Such a schedule would leave no room for Catterall and require the WBA to ignore or alter its previous ruling.

Romero was elevated to Super champion before Catterall defeated Shakhram Giyasov for the WBA’s secondary welterweight title on May 23. The WBA ordered the Super champion to face the winner within a maximum of 180 days, placing the deadline in November.

One voluntary defense has already been granted. Romero used it against Teofimo rather than facing Catterall, and the British southpaw does not believe the new champion should receive another exception.

A fight with the winner of Ryan Garcia versus Conor Benn is Teofimo’s preferred next step, and he has discussed collecting the remaining welterweight belts. Those matches involve more money than a Catterall defense, which explains his preference. Still, taking Romero’s belt also meant inheriting the obligation attached to it.

This is not merely a request for consideration. Catterall holds the secondary belt and has a WBA directive supporting his demand. If the organization enforces its own ruling, three straight unification fights will have to wait.

Teofimo Lopez Wants Three Unifications Without Facing One Mandatory

Teofimo Lopez believes his DAZN contract will take him directly from one welterweight unification to another without stopping for a mandatory defense of his WBA title.

The newly crowned champion is targeting Liam Paro, the winner of Ryan Garcia versus Conor Benn, and eventually Devin Haney. If Lopez gets his way, every appearance during the rest of his deal will involve another champion.

During his post-fight press conference, Lopez said:

“I got three fights with DAZN, and all of them are the road to undisputed. We’re going right to every world title. We’re not taking no title defense, no nothing. Whoever’s next, we’re going for him.”

A unification technically includes a defense of the belts involved, but Lopez’s meaning was clear. He does not plan to face an ordinary mandatory or ranked challenger between attempts to collect the other titles. If that plan proceeds, it will consume well over a year. Each fight requires negotiations between promoters, networks and boxing organizations before the participants complete training camps and recover afterward. Lopez also left the Romero fight with a cut over his right eyebrow that may delay his return.

The first unification depends on another event. Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn are scheduled to fight on September 12, after which the winner will need time to recover and negotiate with Lopez. The next stage against Liam Paro or Devin Haney requires another lengthy round of discussions.

Completing all three fights may leave contenders in several organizations waiting 12 to 18 months. Some will be forced into additional bouts to protect their rankings while the champion moves from one financially attractive unification to another.

Unifications often receive priority because reducing the number of champions is supposed to benefit boxing. That principle becomes difficult to defend when it is used repeatedly to prevent every other challenger from receiving an opportunity.

Granting one exception for a major fight is understandable. Three consecutive exceptions create a separate set of rules for the boxer who generates the most money. Ranked contenders must keep winning while Teofimo remains protected from facing any of them.

The strategy also depends on Lopez winning every fight. A loss transfers the collected titles to another champion, who may then request additional exceptions for more lucrative bouts. The waiting challengers must begin the same process again with someone new.

The schedule Teofimo described requires approval from more than DAZN. The WBA and the other organizations must authorize each step. If they permit three straight unifications without requiring a mandatory defense, the “road to undisputed” will become another example of boxing’s business interests overriding its competitive structure.

Ghana News.title: Ghana’s film industry: The Nokia of African cinema?
Ghana News.content:
There was a time when Ghana was the undisputed giant of filmmaking in West Africa. Long before the rise of Nollywood, Ghanaian productions captivated audiences across the continent. Our films and television dramas were widely watched, our actors were household names, and aspiring filmmakers from neighbouring countries, including Nigeria, crossed our borders to learn the craft.

Today, that situation has dramatically reversed. Nigeria’s Nollywood has become a global brand, ranking among the world’s largest film industries, while Ghana’s once-thriving movie sector struggles for visibility, investment, and market share. The story bears a striking resemblance to that of Nokia, the former king of mobile phones.

When Ghana Was King

In the 1970s, 1980s, and 1990s, Ghana was regarded as a leading centre of film and television production in West Africa. Productions such as Osofo Dadzie, Obra, Things We Do for Love, Ultimate Paradise, Inspector Bediako, and numerous local films dominated screens and captured the imagination of audiences.

At a time when Nigeria’s industry was still developing, many Nigerians came to Ghana to acquire filmmaking skills and technical knowledge. Ghanaian content was broadcast on Nigerian television stations, and Ghana’s filmmakers were respected across the region. Like Nokia in the mobile phone industry, Ghana was ahead of the competition. Nokia’s phones were everywhere; the company dominated the global market and appeared untouchable.

Similarly, Ghana’s film industry occupied a leadership position that many believed would continue indefinitely.

The Turning Point

The problem with being a leader is that success can create a false sense of security. When smartphones began transforming the mobile phone industry, Nokia was slow to adapt. The company underestimated the significance of changing consumer preferences, new technologies, and emerging competitors. The same thing happened in Ghana’s film industry.

While Nollywood aggressively expanded production, embraced direct-to-video distribution, built stronger business networks, and later leveraged digital platforms, Ghana’s industry struggled to evolve with the changing landscape.

Instead of building a sustainable ecosystem, the industry became fragmented. Production houses operated largely in isolation or silos, investment declined, distribution networks weakened, piracy flourished, government support remained inconsistent, and training institutions failed to expand at the pace required by the industry.

Ultimately, Nigeria was building an industry, while Ghana was merely producing films. The difference became monumental.

Nollywood’s Rise

Nigeria understood something that Ghana largely overlooked: filmmaking is both an artistic and a business enterprise. Nollywood focused on volume, market penetration, audience development, and distribution. Producers created films that resonated with local audiences while simultaneously targeting the wider African market and the diaspora.

As satellite television expanded and streaming platforms emerged, Nollywood was ready. International platforms such as Netflix and other notable studios began investing in Nigerian content, exposing African stories to global audiences.

Nigeria’s film industry transformed from a local entertainment sector into an international cultural export. Ghana, despite possessing immense talent and storytelling potential, was largely left behind.

The Nokia Syndrome

The lesson from Nokia’s decline is not that the company lacked talent or resources. Rather, Nokia failed to recognise that the industry had changed. The same can be said about Ghana’s film sector.

For years, discussions have focused on a lack of funding, piracy, government neglect, and competition. While these challenges are real, they do not fully explain the decline. The bigger issue is that the industry did not adapt quickly enough to new realities:

Digital distribution

Streaming platforms

Audience analytics

International co-productions

Content marketing

Brand partnerships

Intellectual property monetisation

Global audience targeting

The world changed, but much of Ghana’s film ecosystem continued operating under old assumptions.

Note: The Nokia comparison works best as a metaphor for lost leadership and a failure to adapt. Unlike Nokia, however, Ghana’s film industry decline was also shaped by structural issues: limited financing, weak distribution systems, piracy, inconsistent policy support, and a relatively small domestic market. Factoring in these elements makes the argument much more balanced and credible.

What Exactly Did Ghana Lose?

The loss was not merely economic; it was deeply cultural. In the 1970s, 1980s, and 1990s, Ghanaian stories reflected Ghanaian realities. They preserved our languages, customs, values, humour, and social experiences. The film industry was not just creating entertainment; it was documenting who we were as a people: our architecture, fashion sense, lifestyle, and developmental transitions.

As the industry’s influence declined, Ghana gradually lost a significant portion of its cultural voice in the African media space. Today, many young Africans are more familiar with Nigerian cities, slang, fashion, and cultural references than they are with Ghanaian culture.

This is not because Ghana lacks stories worth telling, but because stories that are not consistently told, produced, and distributed eventually become invisible.

Film is soft power.

Countries use cinema to shape perceptions, influence culture, attract tourism, and promote national identity. Hollywood has done it for America, Bollywood for India, and Nollywood is doing it for Nigeria. Ghana once had that opportunity but failed to maximise it.

The Cost of Nostalgia

One of the greatest dangers facing the Ghana film industry is excessive nostalgia. Industry conversations often begin with phrases such as:

• “Those were the good old days.”

• “We used to be ahead of Nigeria.”

• “Nigerians learned filmmaking from us.”

While these statements contain elements of truth, they do not resolve today’s challenges.

No audience buys a movie ticket because of what happened thirty years ago. Streaming platforms do not invest in content because of past achievements, and no investor funds a project based solely on historical prestige. The market rewards current relevance.

The uncomfortable truth is that audiences do not owe Ghanaian filmmakers their attention simply because Ghana once led the industry. Attention must be earned repeatedly through compelling stories, high production quality, effective marketing, and consistent delivery.

The future belongs to creators who understand today’s audience, not yesterday’s.

Lessons from Nollywood

There is much Ghana can learn from Nollywood’s success:

1. Embrace Entrepreneurship: Many Nigerian filmmakers stopped waiting for perfect conditions. They produced films with available resources, learned from mistakes, reinvested profits, and gradually scaled up their operations.

2. Master Distribution: A great film that nobody sees is a failed business product. Nigerian producers continuously searched for new ways to reach consumers, from VHS tapes, VCDs, and DVDs to satellite television and streaming platforms.

3. Build Stars and Brands: Actors, directors, and production companies became brands. Audiences began following not just individual films, but the people behind them, creating loyalty and sustained demand.

4. Export Aggressively: The industry targeted African markets, diaspora viewers, and international audiences, a strategy Ghana can adopt while maintaining its unique identity.

What Must Change

To remain competitive and relevant, it is worth looking at Nokia’s current trajectory. Nokia did not fade away; it pivoted to focus on developing telecommunication infrastructure, such as 5G and 6G technologies, and partnered with entities like NVIDIA to research semiconductors, a critical technology for the digital era.

If Ghana’s film industry is serious about rebuilding, several foundational changes are necessary:

Develop Stronger Stories: Technology matters, but storytelling matters more. Many modern productions focus heavily on equipment and visual aesthetics while neglecting script development. Investment in screenwriting workshops, script development programmes, and story incubation initiatives is essential.

Build Sustainable Financing: Many filmmakers spend years searching for funding before production even begins. The industry needs private investment, film funds, sponsorships, grants, and public-private partnerships. Without capital, creativity struggles to flourish.

Embrace Digital Distribution: The future audience lives online. Filmmakers must master streaming, video-on-demand platforms, and social media marketing. Producing a film is only half the job; getting it seen is the other half.

Prioritise Professionalism: Investors are attracted to industries that operate professionally. Clear contracts, transparent accounting, project management systems, and strong business practices are just as vital as artistic talent.

Invest in Training: The industry requires a continuous cycle of training for writers, editors, cinematographers, sound designers, producers, visual effects artists, and marketers. Furthermore, strategic international partnerships with countries that have successfully scaled their industries are critically important.

A New Vision for Ghanaian Cinema

The goal should not be to blindly copy Nollywood, nor should it be to simply relive the glory days of the 1990s. The goal is to create a distinctly Ghanaian film industry that competes globally while remaining deeply rooted in local stories.

Ghana’s rich history, diverse cultures, folklore, music, literature, and contemporary social realities provide an endless supply of stories. What is needed is vision:

• Vision to think beyond the next production.

• Vision to build institutions instead of relying solely on individual successes.

• Vision to create an industry rather than a scattered collection of filmmakers.

Conclusion: Why the Nokia Comparison?

The Nokia comparison reminds us that leadership is never permanent. Being first does not guarantee staying first, and past success does not ensure future relevance.

Yet, Nokia’s story also teaches us that even after losing dominance, a brand can restructure, adapt, and find new areas of relevance. The Ghana film industry can do the same.

The talent is still here. The stories are still here. The audience is still here. What remains uncertain is whether the industry can unite around a common vision and adapt to the realities of the twenty-first century.

If it can, the story of Ghanaian cinema will not be one of terminal decline, but one of powerful reinvention. And that may prove to be the most compelling Ghanaian story of all.

By James Aboagye, Film Producer, Scriptwriter, and Film Director

Ghana News.title: British Council supports two Ghanaian creatives for UK cultural exchange opportunities
Ghana News.content:
The British Council Ghana supported two Ghanaian creatives to participate in prestigious international fashion and literature opportunities in the United Kingdom in August 2026.

The beneficiaries were Awura Abena Agyeman, Co-founder and CEO of WEAR Ghana and Republic of Africa, and Emma Ofosua Donkor, writer, cultural curator and Founder of the All-African Women Poetry Festival.

The opportunities formed part of the British Council Ghana and the UK Government’s commitment to strengthening cultural relations between Ghana and the United Kingdom through investment in the creative economy, cultural exchange, market access and international collaboration. The delegates participated in programmes designed to create long-term partnerships, expand professional networks and showcase Ghana’s creative excellence on global platforms.

Before their departure, the delegates engaged in a series of high-level engagements in Ghana, including courtesy visits to the Minister for Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, as well as a range of media engagements aimed at highlighting the significance of the opportunities and the growing influence of Ghana’s creative sector internationally. Upon their return, the delegates are expected to pay a courtesy call on the British High Commissioner to Ghana.

Showcasing Ghanaian fashion on a global stage

Through the British Council’s Creative Growth Programme, Awura Abena Agyeman participated in Africa Fashion Week London (AFWL) 2026, which took place from 17 to 23 August 2026. The opportunity brought together selected fashion entrepreneurs from across Sub-Saharan Africa for industry networking, skills development, peer learning and market access opportunities. AFWL was recognised as the United Kingdom’s largest annual fashion event dedicated to African and African-inspired design.

During the programme, Awura showcased her work to international buyers, media organisations, fashion influencers, investors and industry stakeholders, positioning Ghanaian fashion within global conversations around creativity, entrepreneurship and cultural innovation.

Awura Abena Agyeman was a fashion entrepreneur and creative industry leader whose brand, Republic of Africa, had become an influential platform for celebrating African identity, creating jobs and promoting home-grown talent. A Mandela Washington Fellow and multiple award nominee, she had been recognised among Ghana’s Top 50 Young CEOs and had collaborated with institutions including Harvard Business School and New York University.

Building international literary and cultural partnerships

Emma Ofosua Donkor was selected for Momentum 2026, an international literature delegate programme that took place in Edinburgh during Scotland’s world-renowned festival season. Anchored within the Edinburgh International Book Festival, Momentum brought together cultural leaders from around the world to develop lasting partnerships with Scotland’s literature sector and the wider international cultural community.

The programme was designed to foster collaboration, strengthen professional networks and create opportunities for future partnerships between cultural institutions, festivals and creative practitioners across countries.

Emma Ofosua was an acclaimed writer, cultural curator, performance poet and literacy advocate. She was the author of I Wish You Courage in the Night Season and Founder of the All-African Women Poetry Festival, a British Council and UNESCO-supported platform that amplifies the voices of women poets from across Africa and the diaspora. Through her work as Managing Editor of Hadithi Magazine and creative lead of Tuniq Africa, she continued to champion cultural entrepreneurship, literary development and African storytelling.

Strengthening UK-Ghana creative collaboration

The British Council believed that international cultural exchange played a vital role in supporting the growth and sustainability of Ghana’s creative economy. Previous participants in similar programmes had secured international collaborations, funding opportunities, business partnerships, publishing relationships and expanded market access across the United Kingdom, Europe and beyond.

The participation of Awura Abena Agyeman and Emma Ofosua Donkor reflected the strength, diversity and global potential of Ghana’s creative sector. Their selection provided individual professional development opportunities and created pathways for wider knowledge exchange, industry collaboration and institutional partnerships that benefited Ghana’s fashion, literature and cultural ecosystems.

This was the second time Ghanaian creatives attended these events. The first, under the Momentum delegation in 2023, was represented by Dr Martin Egglewogbe, the creative director of Pa Gya Festival and president of the Writers Project of Ghana, while Edna Asherlina Darkwaa, the founder of Ometsey, a fashion brand in Ghana, attended the 2025 edition of Africa Fashion Week London.

As Ghana continued to position itself as a hub for creativity and cultural innovation in Africa, the opportunities demonstrated the value of sustained international collaboration in advancing the country’s creative industries and expanding global recognition for Ghanaian talent.

Ghana News.title: Trump says Canada wants ‘benefits’ of being US state after trade talks collapse
Ghana News.content:
US President Donald Trump (L), Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney (R).

US President Donald Trump has said Canada wants "the benefits of being a State, without being one" after trade talks between the two countries collapsed late on Friday.

His comments come after negotiations broke down, triggering new 50% US tariffs on a range of Canadian goods, Trump also said American farmers had been charged "massive amounts of Tariffs" for years.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney called the fresh tariffs a "miscalculation" designed to "hurt and divide us".

Carney confirmed he would match Trump's tariffs "dollar-for-dollar" from 8 September, including levies on steel, dairy, appliances and electronics. The US and Canada are now in a trade "war", he said.

"They asked too much and they offered too little," Carney said on Saturday. "You're at war when you get attacked. We got attacked," he added.

Trump's latest comments echo his repeated references to making Canada the "51st state" of America since returning to office, sparking frustration among its leaders and residents.

The collapse of the trade talks upended a deeply integrated trading relationship, with no clear path to resolution.

"We cannot accept what they've offered, and we will not give what they've asked," Carney said.

On Sunday, while speaking to Fox News, Trump said the Canadians were "foolish" to engage in a trade war with the US and think they will "actually win".

Both countries were optimistic of a deal earlier in the week, but talks fell apart after both sides accused the other of making last-minute changes.

The new 50% US tariffs will apply to a range of Canadian goods, in addition to existing US tariffs on Canadian steel, aluminium, automobiles and lumber.

They are limited in scope, covering about $20bn (£15bn; C$28bn) of Canadian imports, or about 5% in total, including wine, dairy, cement, clothing and hockey equipment.

The prime minister said Canada was retaliating "reluctantly" to protect its interests. Details of the counter-measures will be released in the coming days, he said.

Leaders of other federal parties in Canada, including the Conservative opposition, voiced support for the prime minister, as have the leaders of some Canadian provinces.

Tariffs - a tax placed on imports from other countries - have been a key component of Trump's trade policy, with the US president arguing they will boost American manufacturing and create jobs at home.

Critics, however, say tariffs have raised prices for American consumers and have disrupted and damaged the global economy.

Carney's speech on Saturday was his first address to Canadians after he announced late on Friday night that a deal would not be reached, accusing the Americans of making "last-minute changes" that were "unfair" and "uneconomic".

US negotiators, meanwhile, accused Canada of making "new demands and walk backs" on terms which had been previously agreed.

On Saturday, US trade representative Jamieson Greer told Fox News there were no plans to resume talks.

He added that the US had been prepared to cut some of its tariffs on Canada as part of the ill-fated deal.

Carney, however, said the US presented "unacceptable" terms that were too restrictive, including curbing Canada's ability to strike new trade deals with other countries.

He also rejected the assertion that Canada had made last-minute requests: "We clarified what was on offer and were continually disappointed by the answers."

Doug Ford, the leader of Canada's most populous province Ontario, backed Carney and said Trump "can't be trusted".

British Columbia Premier David Eby said the US demand for restrictions on Canada's ability to have other trade deals "would reduce us to the economic equivalent of the 51st state".

"It was never acceptable to Canadians," Eby said.

The Conservative opposition leader Pierre Poilievre also appeared to support Carney, calling the latest US levies "unjustified".

Quebec's premier, Christine Fréchette, warned jobs would likely be lost as a result of the new US tariffs.

"Behind these numbers are real people," she said, vowing to introduce measures to support impacted sectors.

Alberta Premier Danielle Smith, whose oil-rich province has worked to make inroads with the Trump administration, urged both sides to resume talks.

The collapse comes after more than a year of on-again, off-again trade talks, which intensified in recent weeks after a US-imposed deadline to strike a deal or face further tariffs.

The two countries were also engaged in a mandatory review of an existing North American free trade agreement, known as USMCA, with Mexico.

The pact was signed by Trump during his first term to replace the 1994 North American Free Trade Agreement. It underpins $1.6tn (£1.2tn) in annual trilateral trade across Canada, the US and Mexico.

Earlier this summer, Canada and Mexico had formally requested for USMCA to be renewed for another 16 years. The US, however, declined to renew it in its current form.

Asked how Friday's trade talk collapse would impact the North American free trade pact, Carney said it was "certainly not good news".

Ghana News.title: TikTok to pay $400m to US in one of largest child privacy settlements
Ghana News.content:
TikTok has agreed to pay $400m (£293m) to the US to settle a lawsuit alleging its platform violated children‘s privacy, marking one of the largest-ever settlements over the issue.

The deal stems from a 2024 suit by the Department of Justice, under former President Joe Biden, alleging that TikTok and its parent company, ByteDance, collected "vast amounts of data" on millions of users under the age of 13.

Doing so was against the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA), a federal law enacted in 2000. It is the same law that dozens of US states are now suing Meta over.

"Children and parents are better protected today than they were when this case began," Assistant Attorney General Brett Shumate said.

Other companies that have paid penalties to the US government for COPPA violations include Google's YouTube, which paid $170m in 2019, and Epic Games, which paid $275m in 2022.

Meta is also now facing penalties that could exceed hundreds of billions of dollars stemming from COPPA violations alleged by attorneys general of 29 US states. A jury trial in the lawsuit started this week, with the Instagram and Facebook owner accused of targeting child users and profiting from them.

While the TikTok lawsuit predates last year's split of TikTok's US business and operations from its original base of China, the settlement only involves TikTok's operations in China.

ByteDance, which is a privately held company, was most recently valued by investors at $550bn.

Under the terms of the deal, TikTok and ByteDance will immediately pay the DOJ $300m. It will pay another $100m when the government vacates a 2019 consent decree with the Federal Trade Commission.

As part of the agreement, the predecessor to ByteDance, Musical.ly, was required to pay a $5.7m fine for COPPA violations and ensure it sought parental consent for any user aged under 13.

The Justice Department did not detail any action against TikTok on Friday beyond the fine. But the department noted that since it sued the platform, TikTok has "undergone significant changes," including to its ownership, privacy practices and platform controls for young users.

When the lawsuit was filed, attorneys for the US said that more than 170 million teenagers were using TikTok and that the app was "directed to children." Yet it did not effectively verify users' ages or obtain parental consent from underage users.

In 2024, former President Biden pushed for TikTok to be either banned or for the company to divest its US operations. President Donald Trump went on to support the app's divestment, which occurred last year.

Its US operations are now 81% owned by a consortium of investors, while ByteDance maintains a 19% stake.

A representative of TikTok did not respond to the BBC for comment.

Ghana News.title: Asante Kotoko management doesn’t involve me in supporters mobilization – McBrown
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian actress and TV Show Host, Nana Ama McBrown, has called on the management of Asante Kotoko SC to involve prominent personalities in the Ashanti Region in the club’s activities and fan mobilisation efforts.

McBrown, a well-known supporter of the Kumasi-based club, believes that Asante Kotoko can greatly benefit from the involvement of influential personalities across the Ashanti Region if the club’s management takes the initiative to engage them directly.

According to McBrown, despite her role as brand ambassador of Hisense Ghana, a partner of Asante Kotoko, the partnership has not involved the brand as much as she believes it could.

Speaking on Luv Fm’s DriveTime show, she stressed that her willingness to contribute to the club goes beyond her role as a brand ambassador, but said any meaningful engagement must come directly from the club’s management.

“As a brand ambassador for Hisense Ghana, we already support Kotoko, but they haven’t involved us a lot. They already know I’m a supporter of Asante Kotoko.

"Individually, I think that the management has not involved us a lot. If an individual of the team calls me, I won’t take it seriously, but if the management is calling me, I will be here and I will be ready to do something for the club.”

McBrown believes Asante Kotoko should adopt abroader approach by bringing together prominent personalities and influential figures within the Ashanti Region to help promote and mobilise support for the club. She urged the management to create a platform that allows personalities in the region to contribute their influence toward the growth of the club.

“So I am telling the management they should find a way to involve all personalities in the Ashanti Region, just as other clubs in their regions will do.”

For McBrown, the relationship between Asante Kotoko and the people of Kumasi and the wider Ashanti Region is deeply rooted in identity and belonging.

She emphasised that the the club represents ther egion and therefore deserves collective support from its people.

“I believe that Kumasi is us, Kotoko is for us and Kotoko is for us to serve, so we are waiting for that call.”

Her comments come at a time when clubs are desperately in need of publicity to mobilise supporters ahead of the 2026/27 Ghana Premier League which starts on Saturday, September 5, 2026.

Ghana News.title: Frustration builds in Indiana town struggling without power for 12 days
Ghana News.content:
Nearly two weeks after a damaging storm struck her Indiana town, Terry Dubois is among the tens of thousands still without power.

The 77-year-old has been relying on friends to bring her non-perishable food to eat.

Her son brought her a power bank so she can charge her phone and keep in touch with the outside world.

Thankfully, the summer heat hasn't been too punishing, Dubois said, meaning she has not missed her air conditioning too much.

"I've never seen a storm like that in my entire life. Never, never," she tells the BBC.

"It was like a sheer wall of wind," she recalls.

A wave of sudden, severe storms brought flooding and tornadoes to the US Midwest on 11 August, including to Chicago and Indiana, where seven people were killed.

The former industrial town of Gary, which runs along the southern shore of Lake Michigan, was hit particularly hard. Wind gusts peaked at 99mph (159kmh), according to the National Weather Service.

The worst of the storm only lasted five to 10 minutes, but the impacts are lingering 12 days later.

Toppled trees are being removed after the storm

Power has been restored to more than 345,000 customers since the storm struck, but almost 30,000 were still without power as of Sunday morning, according to the area's electrical company Northern Indiana Public Service Company (Nipsco).

In the first few days after the storm, petrol stations, supermarkets and pharmacies were without power, leaving people to survive on what they had.

As the outage stretched into a second week, global food charity World Central Kitchen arrived to help people without access to food.

Power outages are not out of the ordinary for this part of the US. But outages that last more than a week are uncommon.

Once home to the world's largest steel mill, the former industrial heartland of Gary has felt the outage on many fronts. One third of its roughly 70,000 residents live in poverty, according to US Census data.

As well as dealing with storm-damaged properties, residents of the former industrial town have struggled to source food and maintain good hygiene.

There have also been reports of people unable to refrigerate medication and a wheelchair user crawling down their stairs in the absence of working lifts.

At night, some roads have been "pitch black" without working street lights, Gary resident Kyle Allen tells the BBC.

Allen has experienced shorter power outages before, but this time has been different because he has started caring for his 95-year-old father.

As a result, he bought a generator which has been sustaining him and his father since the power failed.

Demond Pompy, who has been grilling food in Gary during the power outage, told Reuters earlier this week that taking a shower and flushing the toilet are things people take for granted, but defiantly added: "One thing about us, we're going to adapt to any situation"

Shatiya Hardin, meanwhile, said the situation has been "absolutely horrible".

"At night we're sweating, we're irritable, we have children to look out for, elderly people who need electricity for oxygen tanks," she told the BBC's US partner CBS.

"It's not OK for us to continually be in survival mode."

Amid mounting frustration, local residents have launched a class-action lawsuit, accusing the utility company Nipsco of failing to manage the trees which brought down the power lines in the storm.

In the lawsuit, resident Jack Tipold said he was in the middle of dental surgery when the power failed.

He said he was forced to abandon the procedure and was discharged without adequate pain medication.

"I had all my teeth removed, and no medication for 48 hours. Let me tell you something, it was a struggle," he told CBS.

Nipsco has denied wrongdoing and said it would "vigorously" defend itself in court.

Faith leaders alarmed by the ongoing outage held a press conference on Saturday outside a local church.

"We come together today with one voice, asking those who have the power... to release the resources to our brothers and our sisters, our mothers and our fathers, because 12 days is long enough," he said, according to the Indianapolis Star.

People have used ice to cool off in Gary

Nipsco said on Sunday it was restoring power to everyone as soon as possible, and estimated Gary would have its electricity restored by Wednesday.

"We recognise how frustrating and difficult it is to be without power for an extended period," the company said in a statement.

Indiana's governor Mike Braun said on Sunday there was "no excuse for these delays".

He has requested a quicker major disaster declaration from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (Fema), which would unlock further help.

With climate change making extreme weather more severe and frequent, such power outages are likely to become a more common problem.

In the meantime, Braun has pushed Nipsco to bring in more crews to get those without power back online: "Put every available resource into the field. Get creative."
