World.title: ISACA Global President Celebrate Nigeria IT Professionals
World.content:
Oluchi Chibuzor

The Global CEO of Information Systems Audit and Control Association (ISACA) , Erik Prusch has praised the resilience of Nigerian IT professionals as the Lagos Chapter of the body marks its 30 years of impactful leadership.

Speaking in Lagos, acknowledged the role the Lagos Chapter has played in setting the standard across Africa.

According to him, “The success that Lagos has had over the last 30 years has really demonstrated what being a chapter in ISACA is and being a leader in a continent such as Africa. It’s an amazing event when you can gain the expertise that we’ve been able to gain within a growing region of the world like this. And the leadership that this part of the world is creating is going to further the global efforts that ISACA has in general. The amazing thing is whether or not we’re talking about artificial intelligence or cyber security or IT audit or privacy or security in general, ISACA leads the way.

“We lead the way in terms of not only the expertise and credentials that we create but by building workforces for tomorrow that allow nations and allow companies to continue to expand because they’re leveraging technology the right way.”

Urging business leaders and regulatory bodies on cyber security and governance issues, Prusch said that they must have the right workforce.

“The message to global leaders, leading organisations, enterprises, companies is that you need to have the right workforce. A workforce that’s trained and has been developed to be able to lead your organisations into the future, that help accelerate your growth and be able to leverage new technologies before they actually come to market,” he said.

On his part, President of ISACA Lagos Chapter, Mr. Justus Osuji, said that the celebration provided an opportunity to reflect on three decades of professional service, leadership, knowledge development and contribution to the growth of information systems audit, cybersecurity, governance, risk, compliance and emerging technology in Nigeria and beyond.

According to him, “The essence of having the ISACA Nigeria chapters is for us to collaborate to come together to expand the reach of ISACA to all parts of Nigeria. That is the essence of the collaboration we are having to enable us to reach out to other locations in Nigeria. All the chapters have their strengths.

“We have the Abuja chapter there that has the central government with them. We have Lagos that has the business hub with them. Port Harcourt has the oil sector with them. So we are collaborating to bring together all these potentials to be able to reach out more to Nigerians.”

World.title: CARSPO 2026: Policing the Path for 2027 Election Security
World.content:
As Nigeria inches closer to the 2027 General Elections, the Nigeria Police Force, in collaboration with Lenders Consult International, is once again convening the Conference and Retreat for Senior Police Officers (CARSPO), this time with electoral security squarely in focus. The sixth edition, holding September 21 to 23, 2026, in Owerri, Imo State, will bring senior police officers together under the theme “Developing a Nigeria Police Roadmap for Effective Management of Security During Elections,” aiming to concretise strategy for protecting voters, personnel and materials ahead of the 2027 general elections. Chiemelie Ezeobi reports

With few months to go before Nigerians return to the polls in 2027, questions of electoral security are once again moving to the front burner and this time, the Nigeria Police Force (NPF) wants a clearer script to follow. Why you may ask?

Every election cycle in Nigeria brings the same anxious question: can the police keep the process safe? So even though Nigeria’s 2027 General Elections may still be some months away, the Nigeria Police Force isn’t waiting to start planning.

Which is why from September 21 to 23, 2026, senior officers will gather in Owerri, Imo State, for the sixth edition of the Conference and Retreat for Senior Police Officers (CARSPO), where the Force in collaboration with Lenders Consult International, hope to hammer out a working roadmap for keeping voters, personnel and materials safe through the next election cycle.

Themed “Developing a Nigeria Police Roadmap for Effective Management of Security During Elections,” CARSPO 2026 will bring together senior police officers, policing experts and relevant stakeholders to examine emerging electoral security challenges and develop practical strategies for safe, peaceful and credible elections.

According to the Force, deliberations at this year’s edition will focus on Intelligence-led Policing, Police-Community Partnerships, digital technologies, Artificial Intelligence, and other contemporary approaches to strengthening police operations before, during, and after elections.

The conference, primarily involving officers of the rank of Commissioner of Police and above, is expected to provide an opportunity for strategic engagement and the development of practical measures to strengthen the Force’s capacity for election security management, and will facilitate the development of actionable strategies for the protection of voters, electoral personnel, candidates, electoral materials and the general public during the 2027 General Elections.

The opening ceremony is scheduled for 10:00 a.m. on Monday, September 21, in Owerri, Imo State.

Announcing the conference, Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, said the Nigeria Police Force remains committed to strengthening strategic leadership, professionalism and operational preparedness towards ensuring a peaceful, safe and secure environment for the 2027 General Elections.

Lenders Consult Reaffirms Commitment

At a press conference held recently at the Force Headquarters, Abuja, to announce the sixth edition of the conference, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Lenders Consult International, Mr Shina Philips, reaffirmed the organisation’s commitment to supporting the Nigeria Police Force in strengthening security arrangements ahead of the 2027 General Elections.

Philips said the organisation’s partnership with the Nigeria Police was aimed at supporting the Force in developing effective strategies to secure the electoral process and maintain public order during the 2027 elections, adding that the conference will provide an opportunity for senior police officers and other stakeholders to deliberate on strategies for effective election security management.

He said the partnership was aligned with the vision of the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, NPM, psc(+), who recently emphasised the critical role of the police in ensuring electoral stability. According to him, the IGP had noted that “stability of the electoral process largely depends on the Police as the lead agency in internal democracy.”

Philips said Lenders Consult International had partnered the Nigeria Police since 2019 to support policing initiatives and promote modern approaches to policing in Nigeria.

Speaking on the organisation’s consistency in sustaining the platform, Philips said: “Since inception, when we first got approval to organise the Conference and Retreat for Senior Police Officers, we have worked to secure sponsorship for every single edition. We consider this our contribution to support the selfless and patriotic work of the Nigeria Police,” he said.

The Lenders Consult CEO also called for greater support for the Nigeria Police from Nigerians, stressing that securing society and maintaining public order should not be left solely to government.

“While commending the government’s efforts, we emphasise that Nigerians need to support the police in fulfilling their constitutional mandate to secure our society and maintain public order,” Philips said.

He noted that the conference had continued to expand its scope and attract international participants, adding that Nigeria, as the “Giant of Africa,” was playing a leading role in the adoption of modern policing methods.

Philips pledged that Lenders Consult International would continue to work with the Nigeria Police authorities to ensure that the conference remained focused on providing practical and cutting-edge solutions to contemporary policing challenges.

He expressed appreciation to the Inspector-General of Police, the Force Management Team and the entire Nigeria Police Force for their continued support for the programme since its inception in 2019. He also thanked the Imo State Governor, Senator Hope Uzodimma, CON, for agreeing to host the conference in Owerri for the third time.

What CARSPO Has Delivered Over the Years

The commitment behind this year’s edition is rooted in a track record built over five previous editions. Since the maiden edition in 2019, hosted by the Lagos State Government, the conference has been held in various locations, including Uyo, Owerri, and Abeokuta, reflecting its national significance and growing institutional acceptance.

Bringing together officers from the rank of Commissioner of Police and above, the retreat has provided a rare opportunity for commanders to engage in peer review and cross-fertilisation of ideas on policing and security challenges.

Through this process, senior officers have been encouraged to critically assess crime patterns, operational gaps, and resource deployment strategies, with an emphasis on daily crime analysis at command levels, improved situation reporting (SITRE), and enhanced analytical capacity that has strengthened decision-making across the Force.

The retreat has also reinforced the importance of evidence-based policing. By focusing on better management of crime scenes, improved intelligence gathering, and the creation of offenders’ registers for profiling, the conference has helped shift policing from reactive responses toward more proactive and intelligence-led operations.

On technology, discussions at the retreat have consistently pushed for the digitalisation of police processes, the strengthening of the Force Intelligence Bureau (FIB), and an overhaul of the Force’s Information and Communications Technology (ICT) Department.

Emphasis on linking police data with other organisations and agencies has improved information sharing and coordination in criminal investigations, while proposals for fusion centres for intelligence integration reflect a growing recognition that modern policing requires collaboration, data analysis, and real-time information exchange.

The retreat has also encouraged capacity-building for policing cyberspace, promoting partnerships with technology companies and specialised agencies to equip officers with the skills needed to combat cyber-related offences.

Community policing has remained a central theme across editions, with the retreat emphasising the need for officers to engage actively with schools, motor parks, housing estates and local associations.

A related outcome has been the push to implement community radio platforms for policing communication, designed to improve information dissemination and strengthen relationships between police and the communities they serve.

The conference has also reinforced discipline and operational accountability within the Force. Regular briefings by the Force High Command, improved information management, and an emphasis on fact verification have strengthened internal communication, while the canvassing for the reintroduction of pocket notebooks and the biometric capture of all police personnel have improved documentation, transparency and identity verification.

The retreat has also encouraged greater caution in the use of social media by officers, recognising the need for responsible communication in an era of rapidly spreading information.

Beyond the Force itself, the conference has encouraged collaboration with agencies such as the Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS) and private sector organisations, including oil and gas associations, to support resource mobilisation, equipment acquisition and operational efficiency.

A Roadmap for 2027

Taken together, these cumulative gains form the backdrop against which CARSPO 2026 is being convened.

With the 2027 General Elections on the horizon, the Force and its long-standing partner are positioning this year’s Owerri retreat not merely as another edition in the series, but as the platform on which senior police leadership will build a concrete, actionable strategy for securing Nigeria’s next electoral cycle, ranging from the protection of voters and electoral personnel to the safeguarding of materials and the wider public, before, during and after the polls.

World.title: All Blacks captain Ardie Savea praises South Africa’s ‘unity’
World.content:
All Blacks captain Ardie Savea has praised South Africa for the “unity” they showed during the Greatest Rivalry series between New Zealand and the Springboks.

The 32-year-old led the Kiwi team to a 33-16 victory against the Boks at Ellis Park over the weekend.

Both Ardie and Springboks captain have developed a firm friendship on and off the pitch.



ARDIE SAVEA PRAISES SOUTH AFRICA

On his social media platforms, Ardie Savea reflected on the All Blacks’ victory against the Springboks at Ellis Park.

Whilst he could’ve used the opportunity to gloat about his team’s sweet victory, the rugby captain showed love and appreciation to South Africa instead.

Ardie posted clips of Springbok fans welcoming and congratulating him, singing the national anthem, and dancing to the unofficial one, Sister Bethina. He also included a clip of Airlink’s double flyover at the stadium as an ode to the Greatest Rivalry series.



In another pic, Ardie’s two youngest children were seen wearing Springbok replica kits

“Unity”, the 32-year-old skipper captioned the touching post.

‘WE RESPECT THE SPRINGBOKS’

Speaking ahead of the match, Ardie Savea revealed his excitement at playing at Ellis Park, which he claimed was one of the “best places you want to play”.

He told the media of the venue: “You run out, you see the Springbok warriors coming out, the crowd … You always get goosebumps when you come play here….As All Blacks, we love those moments.”

He added: “We respect the Springboks and the world-class alpha they are, but I believe we’re just as quality. Hopefully, we go out there and put on a spectacle.



“Every game against the Boks is challenging, and they’re at the peak of their game. It takes you to places where you question yourself, but as an All Black, that’s where you want to be.”

The All Blacks and Springboks will play two more test matches in South Africa, at DHL Stadium and FNB Stadium, over the next two weeks. They will play their final match in the Greatest Rivalry series in the US.

World.title: Rachel John sets tongues wagging with spicy TikToks
World.content:
Rachel John – the woman romantically linked to Siya Kolisi – has set tongues wagging with several spicy TikTok videos

The Dutch influencer – who reportedly began dating the Springbok captain last year – splits her time between SA and the Netherlands.

The brunette is 10 years younger than her rugby star partner.



RACHEL JOHN’S SPICY TIKTOKS SET TONGUES WAGGING

On her TikTok account, Rachel John has shared several humorous, light-hearted and even spicy content.

In one video, Rachel posted a TikTok voiceover in which she was called a “snack” by her partner. In another, the bubbly brunette responded to a call, where the caller claimed: “It’s over. I told my wife”

“Siya said that?”, asked one follower in the comment section.



@racheljohnie Sometimes you just act clueless and move on with your day ♬ original sound – amygingerhart

Interestingly, Rachel and Siya were spotted together a year after he announced his marriage split from his wife of years, Rachel Kolisi.



The Springbok captain has previously admitted to struggling with alcohol abuse, gambling, partying, and even womanising.

LOW KEY ROMANCE?

Rachel John has returned to Amsterdam after her visa recently expired. But the woman linked to Sya Kolisi will likely be back as soon as possible

In April, the 25-year-old touched down in SA, claiming to have been “heartbroken” when she left two months earlier.



During her time in SA, Rahel has enjoyed spending time with Siya in KwaZulu-Natal, where he wrapped up his life to move to Cape Town, where he has signed a contract with the Stormers.

In recent weeks, Rachel and Siya have kept their romance off social media. While they still follow each other on Instagram, they no longer like or comment under each other’s separate posts.

World.title: ‘Bang, bang!’: Former All Black trolls Springbok supporters
World.content:
Former All Blacks player Lima Sopoaga has trolled Springbok supporters after New Zealand beat South Africa at Ellis Park on Saturday, 22 August.

The Kiwis clinched victory in the first of the four test matches in the Greatest Rivalry series.

ALL BLACKS PLAYER TROLLS SPRINGBOK SUPPORTERS

On his Facebook page, Lima Sopoaga revelled in the All Blacks’ defeat of the Springboks at Ellis Park.



The New Zealand-born player used the opportunity to troll South African rugby fans who had predicted that the Kiwis would lose to the back-to-back Rugby World Cup champions.

He shared: “Receipts kept 🤫 Retaliation is a must, ain’t no maybes ifs or buts”.

Just hours earlier, he cheekily posted: “Bang, bang, Good night”.



Ahead of the match, Lima – who will watch the All Blacks play the Lions, and the Boks again next week – called out South Africans who had sent him death threats.

He posted: “Hey guys, just remember it’s just a game. Some of you in my DMs, sending death threats and abusing the crap out of me. Because I said I want my team to win 2-1 in SA. I love a bit of banter and back-and-forth. But come on now, it’s not that deep”

BACK IN SOUTH AFRICA

Lima Sopoaga – who made his debut in Ellis Park in 2015 – is not the only former All Blacks player who is currently in South Africa to watch the Greatest Rivalry series against the Springboks.



Popular players Dan Carter, Richie McCaw, Keven Mealamu and Sean Fitzpatrick are in the country to cheer on their team.

World.title: Elton Jantjies shows love to Gayton after public suport
World.content:
Elton Jantjies has shown love to Minister of Sport, Arts and Culture Gayton McKenzie after they watched the Springboks and All Blacks live in action at Ellis Park over the weekend.

Their meeting comes a year after the Minister praised the former flyhalf, who is currently on a doping ban, for his perseverance.

Elton was handed down a four-year suspension in early 2024. In recent years, his personal life has made headlines for all the wrong reasons.



ELTON JANTJIES AND GAYTON MCKENZIE MEET AT ELLIS PARK

On his social media platform, Elton Jantjies posted a picture of himself and his mother, Elma, meeting Gayton McKenzie at the Springboks test match against the All Blacks at Ellis Park.

The former Springbok flyhalf also posted pics of him meeting former All Blacks Dan Carter and Richie McCaw, who are both in South Africa for the Greatest Rivalry series.

“South Africa”, the 2019 World Cup champion captioned the post.

Elton’s meeting with Gayton comes a year after the Minister praised the rugby player amid ongoing criticism from the public.

He posted: “I don’t care what you write. I will continue to support Elton, I am a God-fearing man, and I know God can change any life just as he changed mine.

He added: “I will never ever cancel any person because judgment belongs to God.”



In the comments section, Elton Jantjies responded: “Got your back”.

Gayton also praised Elton for pursuing a career as a rugby coach.

He continued, “Congratulations, I am proud of you. I can see what you do for rugby and how hard you work for the Game Changers [Elton’s company].

“Forget the naysayers. You keep fighting. I’m behind you. Let me know if you need some help; I’m available”.

Elton reposted the clip on his Instagram with the caption: “A message from a true leader.”

WHAT IS FORMER SPRINGBOK DOING NOW?

In early 2024, Elton Jantjie was given a four-year doping ban by the South African Institute for Drug-Free Sport (SAIDS) after he tested positive for clenbuterol from a sample taken a year earlier

At the time, he had been linked with a possible return to the Lions.

He will be eligible to play professionally again in 2028.

In the interim, Elton has been keeping himself occupied with his rugby school, Game Changers, and various endorsement deals.

He told Behind The Ruck last year: “I’m very busy in terms of my own individual development. Staying fit and healthy.

“A lot of guys were in my position; they probably would have shot themselves or committed suicide. Or they would have gone off the rails, you know. But I just keep doing what I’m doing. What makes me healthy and puts me at peace, and where everybody smiles.”

World.title: Siya Kolisi’s cute big brother moment at Phelo’s Matric Dance
World.content:
A video of Springbok Siya Kolisi jokingly playing a strict big brother at his ster Phelo’s Matric Dance has gone viral on TikTok.

The Springbok captain has two younger siblings, whom he and his former wife, Rachel Kolisi, became legal guardians over after their mother’s death.

In a video posted on her TikTok account, Phelo, the sister of Siya Kolisi, shared a look at her Matric Dance that took place earlier this year.



In the clip, Phelo and her date pose for photos alongside her rugby-star sibling.

Siya quickly went into big brother mode, jokingly demanding that Phelo’s date keep a safe distance from her.

She captioned the clip: “My brother said, ‘Not on my watch’”.



Take a look…

On her Instagram account, Phelo posted pics of her “unforgettable” Matric Dance experience, where both Siya and Rachel Kolisi were present.

MOTHER FIGURE

Despite their divorce, Siya Kolisi’s ex-wife, Rachel Kolisi, has taken on a motherly role for his younger siblings, Phelo and Liyema.



The former couple adopted his siblings, who had been placed in foster care in Zwide following their mother’s death, after an 18-month legal process.

At the time, Rachel was just 24 years old and had her own child, a son named Nicholas.

While Liyema has now come of age, Phelo still lives with Rachel and her two children with Siya in their Cape Town family home.

World.title: Livid Springbok fan crashes out at Ellis Park: ‘You dropped us!’ [video]
World.content:
A rugby fan crashed out after watching the Springboks lose to the All Blacks at Ellis Park. Images via TikTok

A Springbok fan who watched South Africa lose to the All Blacks at Ellis Park has put the team on blast in a viral video.

The Boks lost 33-16 in their first of four test matches in the Greatest Rivalry series

New Zealand have been on a winning streak, whilst in the country, also beating provincial clubs, the Sharks, Bulls and Stormers.



SPRINGBOKS SUPPORTER AT ELLIS PARK PUTS TEAM ON BLAST

On TikTok, a video of a Springbok supporter ranting about spending a small fortune to watch the team play – and lose to the All Blacks has gone viral.

The unidentified man told content creator @fredandrods of the experience: “Well played All Blacks. But f**k you Springboks, if you can drop us like that at Ellis Park. The All Blacks have never [dropped their fans] at Eden Park

The man added that he had paid thousands for his ticket.



He added, “Look at that crowd, they had every supporter. Number one in the world!”

In the comment section, many Springbok fans agreed…

Meelz: “Valid crash out—paying 1.5k only to watch the boys lose LIVE”



Ninjurrr: “As a paying fan, it’s valid”

Renier Robbertse: “As a nation, they did let us down. should never have happened!”

Tesle: “Crying in Rands!”

TICKET PRICES FOR THE GREATEST RIVALRY

The Springboks will play their second and third test matches against the All Blacks at the DHL Stadium and FNB Stadium, respectively.



According to Ticketmaster, there are no available tickets for next week’s game in Cape Town on 29 August. However, fans can expect to pay between R1650 and R4 000 for a ticket to watch the rugby rivals on 5 September.

SA Rugby has warned the public not to bank on purchasing discounted ticket prices for Springbok home games, as was done with Ellis Park and other test matches.

A spokesperson said: “This is not a precedent for future seasons, but a response to market conditions with the sole aim of generating as much support as possible for the Springbok team”.

World.title: DA mourns death of eThekwini councillor Welekazi Sibiya
World.content:
The Democratic Alliance (DA) in KwaZulu-Natal has announced the death of eThekwini Metro councillor Welekazi Sibiya following a short illness.

The party confirmed Sibiya’s death on Sunday, 23 August, with provincial leader Sithembiso Ngema describing her passing as a major loss for the DA and KwaZulu-Natal.

DA mourns Welekazi Sibiya

Ngema said Sibiya had served the party and residents of eThekwini with commitment and had built a reputation for challenging the municipality on issues affecting communities.



He described her as a dedicated young leader whose contribution to public life had been cut short.

“We have lost a colleague, a public representative and, above all, a leader who still had so much to give,” Ngema said.

The party said Sibiya had shown courage in holding the eThekwini administration accountable and remained committed to serving residents.



Ngema said her death was a “tremendous loss” to the DA, eThekwini and KwaZulu-Natal.

Sibiya had risen through DA ranks

Sibiya had become a prominent figure within the DA’s eThekwini structures.

Earlier this year, she contested the position of DA KwaZulu-Natal provincial chairperson against Public Works and Infrastructure Minister Dean Macpherson at the party’s provincial congress.



Her work in the metro also included serving in the Economic Development and Planning portfolio. She had previously held the position of deputy whip of the municipality’s Economic Development and Planning Committee.

Sibiya was also vocal on governance and service delivery matters in the city and had previously raised questions over municipal spending and decision-making.

Tributes pour in

Public Works and Infrastructure Minister Dean Macpherson also paid tribute to Sibiya following news of her death.



“It is with deep sadness that we mourn the passing of eThekwini Councillor, Welekazi Sibiya after a short illness,” Macpherson said.

He extended condolences to Sibiya’s partner, children and family.

The DA said it would remember Sibiya for her commitment to public service and her determination to hold those in power accountable.

World.title: Du Noon horror: Police seek answers after grisly discovery
World.content:
Police are seeking answers after a disturbing discovery involving four people in Du Noon, Cape Town, on Sunday. Image: Flickr

Milnerton police responded to the N7 off-ramp on Malibongwe Drive in Du Noon, where officers made the gruesome discovery in an open field next to the road.

All four victims had been burnt beyond recognition.

Tyres allegedly used to set victims alight

In a statement, Western Cape police spokesperson Sergeant Wesley Twigg said evidence at the scene indicated that tyres had been used to set the victims alight.



“Determinations was made based on the crime scene that tyres were used to set the victims alight. The circumstances surrounding the crime incident remain unclear and the motive is yet to be determined,” Twigg said.

Detectives from the Serious Violent Crime Unit are investigating the Du Noon murders.

Police appeal for information

Police have appealed to the public for information that could help detectives establish what happened and identify those responsible.

Anyone with information can contact Crime Stop on 08600 10111 or submit a tip through the MySAPS App.

The investigation continues.

World.title: From Broken Services to Accountability: ANC's Manifesto Promises Municipal Renewal
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG – ANC president Cyril Ramaphosa has admitted to his party’s failures over the years but has promised South Africans that they will do better.

Ramaphosa was unveiling the ANC’s six-point turnaround plan to win back votes ahead of the 2026 Local Government Elections.

South Africans head to the polls on 4 November.

“We have now built millions of houses. We have laid kilometers and kilometers of water pipes and electricity lines. We have constructed roads; we have built clinics, hospitals, schools, colleges and universities and opened opportunities that did not exist before for people of our country.

“Much of this progress has been achieved through an ANC-led government.

“We must also speak with honesty: in too many municipalities, comrades, services are unreliable. Infrastructure is deteriorating and communities wait too long to have their problems solved.

“There are water treatment plants that are not properly maintained; the pipes that should deliver and transport the water are aging and are deteriorating, which is a continuous problem.

“Streetlights that remain broken and refuse that is not collected.

“There are municipalities, we must admit, that are in financial trouble. There are municipalities that have been weakened by poor leadership, political instability, corruption and the appointment of people who do not have the skills required for the work that they must perform.

“Now, as the ANC, we comrades accept responsibility both for the progress that has been made, but we also accept responsibility for the failures and shortcomings where we govern.

“We will not mince our words and we will not run away from the reality that confronts our people. We will not seek to explain away the frustration of our people. We feel our people's frustration. We will not dismiss the anger that our people feel. We will not ask communities to accept our excuses where they have a right to expect us to do more,” he said.

He said if citizens vote them into power, work will begin immediately after election day.

“The work will begin on the first day after the election. We are going to clock it. We're going to clock it. ANC mayors and councilors must publish their priorities. They must establish service delivery baselines and show measurable progress on the most urgent problems facing the communities.

“The 2026 local government manifesto of the African National Congress includes a tracking mechanism through which councillors will account for implementation. Yesterday I said this mechanism is going to be like a radar screen where you see everything that's happening in our municipalities.

“That just goes to show the level of seriousness by the African National Congress on ensuring that this time around, we are serious about rebuilding our municipalities.”

Here are the six priorities the ANC promises to focus on:

World.title: ‘Manifestos don’t win elections’ - political analyst
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Political analyst Bheki Mngomezulu believes election manifestos are overrated and have little influence on voters.

He said they have become little more than a tick-box exercise.

Mngomezulu said many voters make decisions without reading manifestos, while others choose their party long before election day.

His comments came as the ANC launched its election manifesto in Johannesburg.

READ: 'Victory or death' – Malema tells supporters at the EFF election manifesto launch

“Manifestos don't win elections. And I base that argument on the fact that there are people who vote for political parties having not read even one word of the manifesto.

“I'm not talking about the first sentence or first paragraph, just one word of the manifesto, but they still vote for the party anyway. And then there are those who tell themselves long before the election that I will never vote for party X, whatever X stands for.

READ: DA launches election manifesto

“So it doesn't really matter how much time you put into crafting a manifesto. The reality is that people will vote for other reasons other than reading the manifesto.

“As for the ANC, yes, indeed, the ANC has commanded support in the country since 1994, but their support has been waning in each and every election. And there are a number of reasons for that, which you can talk about at a later stage. But the reality is that what the ANC is doing is what other political parties are doing, which is basically an exercise that, before an election, you launch a manifesto where you promise people what you are going to do,” Mngomezulu said.

READ: UDM launches election manifesto

He questioned what new thing the was the ANC was going to do now that they had been unable to do before.

“Those are some of the questions that are more critical for me, which is why last week I was talking at another event and I said, if I had it my way, those parties that have been in the game for too long should not be launching manifestos because we already know what they're capable of. We also know what their weaknesses are,” added Mngomezulu.

World.title: Lindsay Clancy triple-murder trial nears conclusion
World.content:
MASSACHUSETTS - The defence has rested in the murder trial of an American woman accused of murdering her three children, after claiming she was suffering from postpartum psychosis.

Lindsay Clancy’s lawyers do not dispute that she killed her three children at their home in Massachusetts.

They said she did so because of a severe mental illness, and that she experienced hallucinations of a voice telling her to do so.

Ahead of the defence resting its case on Friday, Clancy’s lawyers sought to strengthen their argument that the 36-year-old killed her children in January 2023 because she was suffering from postpartum psychosis by questioning more of her family members about her mental state at the time.

Clancy’s mother told the court that in December 2022, while also in the presence of her husband, “She told us she had thoughts of harming the children.”

A psychologist who treated Clancy in hospital after the killings told the court that she had a mental disease or defect.

Meanwhile, prosecutors said the former labour and delivery nurse is guilty of murder because she planned the killings rationally and made sure her husband was out of the house when she choked her children, aged five, three and eight months.

The case has drawn significant attention online and has also seen hundreds of people, mostly women, many dressed in pink, turn up outside the Massachusetts court to support Clancy.

The groups said they are trying to raise awareness of how the mental health system treats women.

Many wore clothing with phrases such as “Believe”, “She Needed Help” and “Peace for Lindsay”.

The trial has also drawn TikTok and social media commentators spreading conspiracy theories about the case.

These include a theory that her former husband, Patrick, who has not been charged with any crime, was involved.

On Friday afternoon, prosecutors began calling “rebuttal witnesses” and are expected to make their closing arguments next week.

The case has received international attention, and the final days of the trial are being watched closely around the world.

World.title: ‘I'm absolutely livid’ - Cachalia on IDAC corruption exposed at Madlanga Commission
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia is outraged by the extent of corruption exposed at the Madlanga Commission involving IDAC.

The revelations that the NPA unit was used to target innocent people have been deeply disheartening for Cachalia.

On Friday, the NPA unconditionally withdrew charges against Crime Intelligence head Dumisani Khumalo, Dineo Mokwele and several others.

“So, some charges have been withdrawn against General Khumalo, for instance. That was the outcome of a review process initiated by the head of the NDPP, Andy Mothibi. I'm waiting for that process to be concluded before it is clear what other steps need to be taken.

“But I have to say, what I see being under scrutiny before the Madlanga Commission at IDAC, you know, I just feel complete outrage.

“People in positions of leadership have behaved with a shocking combination of incompetence, at the very least. But clearly there are suggestions that there were ulterior purposes. The damage that they have done to the fight against corruption is enormous. I'm absolutely livid."

World.title: ‘We want the mastermind’ - Deokaran family
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Who paid for the hit on Babita Deokaran?

That's the question that continues to plague the family and friends of the anti-corruption whistleblower.

Today marks five years since Deokaran was gunned down outside her home.

She was killed for uncovering suspicious and irregular payments at Tembisa Hospital, totalling over R850 million.

READ: ‘People who benefited from her death are in power’ - Cachalia on Deokaran murder

Her work helped expose what became a much larger corruption scandal.

Her brother, Rakesh Deokaran, said their focus is not on the people already in the dock for her murder.

"We are not interested in the six arrested. We want the mastermind. A hitman doesn't hire himself. It's unfortunate that, five years later, by her not being here, they thought it was the end. Unfortunately for them, we did not stay quiet,” he said.

World.title: ANC launches election manifesto in Diepsloot
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The ANC manifesto will address lessons learnt and come up with better solutions.

That's the promise from provincial convener and Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi.

The party is launching its manifesto in Diepsloot faced with declining support,

and unhappiness over lack of services.

Party Gauteng provincial convener Panyaza Lesufi said the manifesto shows that they have learned from their mistakes.

"This manifesto will see the hallmark of it is to say we have learned from our mistakes. The hallmark of it is that we have accepted the limitations, the capacity, the leadership that we have deployed and some of the municipalities need assistance.

“And Emfuleni is high on the agenda. But take the 11 municipalities that are in Gauteng. If you isolate Emfuleni in Merafong, we've got nine solid municipalities that are run by the African National Congress in partnership with other coalition partners.

“That alone demonstrates the desire, the ability, the skill and the talent for us to run these municipalities.

“There's a municipality, it's a stone's throw away, called Rand West, with two consecutive clean audits. The ability to know where you have made a mistake will be demonstrated here, where the President outlined that we know where we have made a mistake at leadership level, at infrastructure level, at capacity level, and therefore this manifesto that we are launching today is rectifying those limitations,” Lesufi said.

World.title: ‘People who benefited from her death are in power’ - Cachalia on Deokaran murder
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The masterminds behind the brutal murder of anti-corruption whistleblower Babita Deokoran are free because they are in positions of power.

That's the view of acting police minister Firoz Cachalia.

Today marks five years since Deokoran was gunned down outside her home for uncovering widespread looting at Tembisa hospital.

“The people who benefited financially from her death, and the reason why we don't have justice, is because those people are in power and can protect themselves. That problem of corruption is the disease and illness eating at our country’s hopes,” Cachalia said.

World.title: Gauteng PKTT arrests five Emfuleni Municipality employees
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Five employees of Emfuleni Municipality have been arrested in connection with allegations of fraud, theft and tampering with essential infrastructure.

The arrests, conducted by Gauteng's Political Killings Task Team, follow Friday's takedown operation in Vanderbijlpark.

The suspects are attached to the Revenue and Electrical Departments.

Preliminary investigations indicate that the suspects operated a scheme in which they misrepresented themselves to municipal clients as authorised officials who could reconnect electricity supplies.

Clients were then allegedly instructed to pay various amounts of money directly into the suspects’ bank accounts.

The five arrested suspects are expected to make their first appearance in court tomorrow.

World.title: Uhuru: Don't claw back our freedoms as political intolerance grows
World.content:
Dr. Fred Matiangi,Eugene Wamalwa & Former president Uhuru Kenyatta with opposition leaders during the 24rd anniversary for former Vice President Kijana Wamalwa. [Osinde Obare, Standard]

Retired President Uhuru Kenyatta has scoffed at ongoing attempts to disrupt and sow chaos in opposition rallies while addressing residents at the memorial of late Vice President Kijana Wamalwa.

In likely reference to the ongoing problem of goons, the former president said the growing intolerance and disruption of meetings is taking Kenya backwards. He challenged politicians to seek votes in peace.

World.title: Ndindi Nyoro begins nationwide political mobilisation ahead of 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro after attending service at Gathuki-ini ACK Church on August 23, 2026. [Boniface Gikandi, Standard]

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro has said he will take his campaign for national transformation across Kenya as he positions himself for the 2027 presidential race.

Ndindi said he was interested in leadership committed to addressing concerns in education, health, youth and unemployment, among other needs.

Nyoro, who is the People’s Party of Kenya leader, spoke at St Michael Gathuki-ini ACK Church in Kiharu on Sunday, where he called for respect and political maturity.

Addressing residents in Kiria-ini (Mathioya) and Gakira (Kangema), he urged politicians to engage in a responsible manner.

“I trust in God that after next year Kenya will be able to have leadership that will be responsible for improving citizens' standards of living,” he said.

He regretted that hundreds of university graduates in the area were yet to secure employment.

“I plead with Kenyans to support my course that is geared to transform the nation and ensure equality and transparency,” said the PPK leader.

Nyoro said that after engaging Murang'a residents, he will take his transformation campaigns to all parts of the country.

Speaking at Kiria-ini market, he said he would engage the people to seek their blessings.

“All along had been feeling the urge to lead the country, thus the need to come out in the open and fight for position,” he said.

On Monday, the MP announced his exit from the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA), declaring that he will join the opposition ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Nyoro, an economist serving his second term as Kiharu MP, said he will work with opposition leaders to push for what he termed real change in Kenya.

The legislator said all opposition presidential aspirants are welcome at rallies organised by the PPK.

His move marks a significant political shift as parties and leaders begin positioning themselves ahead of the 2027 polls.

World.title: City Hall in rush to expand drainage system ahead of El Nino
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja during an inspection tour of the ongoing drainage system expansion. [GPS]

Nairobi County has embarked on drainage expansion works aimed at mitigating floodwaters ahead of El Nino rains.

Governor Johnson Sakaja, while calling on city residents to remain alert and proactive, said City Hall has intensified preparations and accelerated identification of hotspots.

The governor on Friday said his administration is taking early and coordinated action to minimise the impact of heavy rains, urging residents to stay calm, pay attention to official information and follow guidance from the multi-agency team established to coordinate the city’s preparedness and emergency response.

“We are working proactively to address the challenges of flooding before El Nino hits the ground. We urge our people not to panic but to be alert and get information from our multi-agency team,” said Sakaja.

The Governor spoke during an inspection tour of several flood-prone areas in Nairobi, including the Mombasa Road-Bunyala Junction corridor and Globe Roundabout, which experienced significant flooding during previous heavy rains.

Sakaja said drainage works are already underway in the affected areas, with teams working to open up and deepen drainage channels, clear obstructions, and improve storm-water flow to prevent a repeat of the flooding witnessed previously.

His remarks come as weatherman warned of increased rainfall in the coming months, with Nairobi among the urban areas requiring heightened preparedness because of its exposure to flooding and the impact of heavy rainfall on roads, settlements and other critical infrastructure.

Sakaja said the county has so far brought together the disaster management teams, Kenya Red Cross, Kenya Urban Roads Authority (KURA) and Kenya National Highways Authority (KeNHA) under a coordinated programme worth Sh2.4 billion to strengthen Nairobi’s flood resilience.

Of the amount, Sh2 billion has been set aside for drainage and flood-mitigation works targeting 19 roads in flood-prone areas.

The projects are at an advanced stage, with tenders awarded and contractors expected to commence implementation after completion of the necessary processes.

Sakaja reiterated that the programme will complement ongoing county interventions under the Nairobi Regeneration Programme, which includes the rehabilitation and upgrading of critical infrastructure across the city.

“The Sh2 billion will support a comprehensive drainage overhaul that complements the ongoing Nairobi Regeneration Programme. Our goal is to permanently address the flooding challenges that have affected the city for many years,” Sakaja said.

He said the focus is not only on responding to floods after they occur, but on addressing the infrastructure weaknesses that have historically made Nairobi vulnerable to flooding.

To strengthen preparedness, the county has established five specialised sub-committees under the multi-agency framework.

The committees include Infrastructure and Drainage; Emergency Response and Evacuation; Shelter and Relief; Security and Traffic and Communication.

While the Infrastructure and Drainage committee will coordinate the clearing and improvement of drainage systems, rivers and other critical infrastructure, the Emergency Response and Evacuation committee will oversee rapid response, rescue and evacuation operations whenever emergencies occur.

The Shelter and Relief committee will prepare safe shelters and coordinate the provision of food, water, medical assistance and other essential support to affected residents.

The Security and Traffic committee will coordinate security, traffic management and emergency access, while the Communication committee will strengthen early-warning systems, public alerts and timely dissemination of information.

Sakaja said the county is also mobilising personnel, equipment and other resources to clear blocked drains, remove silt and waste and strengthen emergency response systems in areas identified as vulnerable.

He urged residents and their associations, businesses and other stakeholders to play an active role in flood preparedness by keeping drainage areas clear and paying attention to official warnings.

The county chief said residents in high-risk areas will be provided with timely information on emerging weather conditions and the actions they should take when heavy rains occur.

“We don’t want people to panic. We want people to be proactive, to listen to information and to work with us. The multi-agency team is in place, and we are preparing before the rains intensify,” Sakaja said.

According to him, the multi-agency approach will also help eliminate jurisdictional gaps by bringing together national and county agencies to operate as one coordinated team.

He said the combination of drainage upgrades, emergency preparedness, early-warning systems and coordinated response would strengthen Nairobi’s resilience and reduce disruption caused by heavy rains.

The multi-agency team is expected to meet next week to review progress, coordinate ongoing works and further push the city’s El Niño preparedness agenda.

World.title: Public officers eyeing elective posts to resign by February 10 - IEBC
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon addressing the press at a past press conference. [File, Standard]

Public officers seeking to contest elective positions in the 2027 General Election have until February 10, 2027, to resign from office, the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has announced.

IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon said the deadline falls exactly six months before the August 10, 2027, General Election, which the Commission has confirmed will be held on a Tuesday.

“Any public officer who intends to contest in this election must resign from public office by Wednesday, 10th February 2027, which is exactly six months before the election,” Ethekon said.

The IEBC said adherence to the timelines will be non-negotiable, noting that they are legally binding and essential to ensuring an orderly electoral process.

Under the timetable, political parties must submit their membership lists and details of candidates participating in party primaries by March 16, 2027.

Party primaries and any related disputes must be concluded by May 8, while independent candidates are also required to meet their legal obligations by the same date.

Presidential aspirants will have until May 24 to submit lists of supporting voters drawn from a majority of Kenya’s counties.

Candidate registration will begin on May 29, with specific deadlines applying to the various elective positions.

The official campaign period will commence after candidates are registered, but not earlier than May 29, 2027.

Ethekon warned political parties, candidates and their supporters against breaching the prescribed campaign period, saying any electioneering outside the legal window will be unlawful.

The restrictions cover campaign posters, billboards, political caravans and other forms of campaigning.

Campaigning will close on August 7, 2027, 48 hours before Kenyans head to the polls.

“The law prescribes when election campaigns may commence,” Ethekon said, urging political parties, candidates and their supporters to strictly comply with electoral laws and regulations.

The deadline is among key milestones unveiled by the electoral commission as political parties, aspirants and other stakeholders begin preparations for the next General Election.

World.title: Schools will open on August 24 as scheduled, Ogamba says
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Students heading home during recent demonstrations. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The Ministry of Education said the official academic calendar remains unchanged.

In a statement issued on Wednesday, August 19, Education Cabinet Secretary Julius Ogamba insists that learners will return to school on Monday, August 24, 2026.

The CS has dismissed reports circulating on social media claiming that the reopening of schools for the third term has been postponed, warning parents, teachers, learners and education stakeholders against relying on unauthorised online notices.

“We wish to clarify that the academic calendar for Basic Education institutions and Teacher Training Colleges remains unchanged,” the CS said.

The clarification comes two days before the scheduled reopening of schools, amid reports circulating on social media platforms suggesting that the government had pushed back the start of Term III.

"Our attention has been drawn to misleading information circulating on various social media platforms, purporting that the academic calendar for basic education institutions and Teachers Training Colleges has been changed," he stated.

The Ministry termed the reports “FALSE” and urged members of the public to completely disregard them.

Ogamba said the Ministry had directed Regional Directors of Education, County Directors of Education and Sub-County Directors of Education to ensure strict compliance with the approved academic calendar contained in a circular dated October 9, 2025.

According to the Ministry, pre-primary, primary, junior, senior and secondary schools will begin Term III on Monday, August 24. The term will run for nine weeks and end on October 23, 2026.

The reopening marks the final academic term of the school year, with schools expected to implement the approved programmes as they prepare learners for the end-of-year national assessments and examinations.

Diploma Teachers Training Colleges will also resume academic operations on August 24, with their third term scheduled to conclude on November 6, 2026.

The Ministry further confirmed that the national assessment and examination calendar has not been altered for KPSEA, KILEA, KJSEA, KPLEA and KCSE are scheduled to begin from October 26, 2026, as earlier announced.

The Ministry also reminded schools that extracurricular activities and visits to secondary schools will remain banned during Term III.

The latest clarification is part of efforts by the government to prevent confusion among parents, learners and teachers as schools prepare to reopen.

Ogamba urged education stakeholders to obtain information through official Ministry communication channels, rather than social media posts whose authenticity cannot be established.

“Parents, teachers and learners and members of the public are advised to strictly rely on the Ministry's official communication channels and field officers for accurate information," he said.

World.title: Ruto denies Sh104bn SHA technology contract
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto has dismissed claims that the government entered into a controversial Sh104 billion contract with Safaricom and Apeiro Limited for the Social Health Authority (SHA) technology system.

Speaking on Tuesday evening at the Presidential Townhall held during the National Health Summit at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC) in Nairobi, Ruto defended the government's investment in digital health, saying the technology was designed to improve transparency and accountability in the management of SHA services.

“There is no Sh104 billion contract. What we have done is design a digital system to make sure that everything is visible. Every treatment must be traceable, and every payment must be accounted for,” Ruto said.

He explained that the government had not purchased the technology outright but had engaged investors who own the equipment, with the State paying for the services provided.

His remarks were echoed by Digital Health Agency Chief Executive Anthony Lenaiyara, who rejected claims that SHA had committed Sh104 billion to technology upgrades.

“It is not correct or true that SHA has undertaken any upgrade or invested Sh104 billion in technology upgrades. What we did is build a digital superhighway comprising 43 systems to support Universal Health Coverage,” Lenaiyara said.

Lenaiyara said the technology infrastructure had been rolled out without requiring health facilities to purchase the devices, adding that the system had transformed the processing and accountability of SHA claims.

He contrasted the new system with the former National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF) model, where claims were processed using physical files that moved between different offices for verification and approval.

Ruto also addressed other government programmes, saying the State had mobilised resources to construct 23,000 additional classrooms to ease pressure caused by shortages of learning spaces.

World.title: 'That was not healthcare, it was theft'- Ruto on old health system
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during the official opening of the Kenya Health Summit at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC), Nairobi, August 18,2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has accused the defunct National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF) system of enabling theft from sick Kenyans, citing claims for procedures that never happened.

Speaking on Tuesday, August 18, at the opening of the Kenya Health Summit at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC) in Nairobi, Ruto described the old system as opaque and vulnerable to abuse.

"We heard of claims for procedures that never happened, fictitious patients and inflated bills. That was not healthcare, it was theft, and theft from sick Kenyans," said Ruto.

He called digital health systems the backbone holding the reforms together and said they would close loopholes that let people profit from the system's weaknesses.

Ruto ranked Universal Health Coverage (UHC) alongside the Affordable Housing Programme as one of the government's most consequential social transformation efforts, crediting collaboration between national and county governments for changes in how healthcare is financed, delivered and accounted for.

The two-day summit, themed "Reforms Delivered, Health as a Right," has drawn more than 5,000 delegates to audit progress under the Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda (BETA) and set priorities for the remainder of Ruto's term, according to Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale.

Ruto said 32.3 million Kenyans are now registered with the Social Health Authority (SHA), which replaced NHIF in October 2024.

Eight million have received treatment, more than 1.2 million mothers have been supported to deliver safely and more than 500,000 surgical procedures have been supported, he added.

He put Kenyans' previous annual out-of-pocket health spending at Sh150 billion ($1.16 billion), saying families had borrowed, sold assets or organised harambees to cover medical costs before the reforms.

"Millions paid out of pocket, borrowed, sold assets, organised harambees or stayed away from hospital because they could not afford care," said Ruto.

Since October 2024, SHA has received more than Sh209 billion ($1.62 billion) and paid more than Sh178 billion ($1.38 billion) to contracted facilities across all 47 counties, Ruto added.

He credited 107,800 Community Health Promoters, deployed under a shared financing arrangement between national and county governments, with reaching more than nine million households and referring over 750,000 people for further treatment.

On supply chains, Ruto said the Kenya Medical Supplies Authority's (KEMSA) fill rate had risen from about 40 per cent to 91 per cent, helped by a Sh1.5 billion ($11.6 million) recapitalisation and a Sh10 billion ($77.4 million) credit line.

The reforms rest on four laws Ruto signed on 19 October 2023: the Primary Health Care Act, the Social Health Insurance Act, the Digital Health Act and the Facilities Improvement Financing Act.

Ruto acknowledged gaps remained in registration, benefit clarity, claims processing and digital systems.

"The ultimate measure of reform is not the laws we pass or the numbers we register, but the experience of the patient in terms of dependable, affordable and dignified care," said Ruto.

Deputy President Kithure Kindiki, Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi, National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula, Duale and Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja attended the opening session, alongside county governors, principal secretaries, members of Parliament and development partners.

The summit runs through Wednesday.

World.title: Gachagua: Opposition does not need Uhuru's money to send Ruto home
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua during a church service at PCEA Rev. Samuel Marima Memorial Church in Gatundu South, Kiambu on August 16, 2026. [Kimaku Chege, Standard]

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed claims that former President Uhuru Kenyatta is financing opposition activities against President William Ruto.

Addressing the allegations that Kenyatta was financing opposition campaigns, Gachagua insisted that the movement did not require money from the former President.

Gachagua says the movement seeking political change is driven by Kenyans and does not depend on financial sponsorship.

“Nasikia kwamba Uhuru is sponsoring us to campaign against you. Uhuru is not sponsoring us, we don't need any sponsorship, this is a mass movement for change which does not need funding,” he said.

He was speaking on Sunday, August 16, 2026, during a church service at PCEA Rev. Samuel Marima Memorial Church in Gatundu South, Kiambu County.

Gachagua further said the opposition had sufficient public support to challenge the Kenya Kwanza administration ahead of the 2027 General Election, insisting that Kenyans themselves were the driving force behind calls for a change of government.

He added that the public itself would determine the political fate of the Ruto administration.

“We don't need money but Kenyans will send you home,” Gachagua said.

The comments come against the backdrop of renewed debate over political alliances and the role of former leaders in Kenya's 2027 succession politics. Kenyatta, who served as President from 2013 to 2022, has largely remained outside the day-to-day administration of government since handing over power to Ruto.

Gachagua also defended Kenyatta against what he described as attempts to drag the former President into the current political contest.

“Uhuru Kenyatta asiguzwe na mtu yeyote. Alindwe na atetewe na apatiwe amani. Uhuru alifanya kazi yake na akastaafu,” Gachagua said.

The former Deputy President said Kenyatta should not be treated as a political candidate or blamed for the activities of opposition politicians.

“Nimemwambia Ruto unauliza Uhuru nini na sio candidate in the next election. I am your main opponent,” Gachagua said.

His remarks came amid an increasingly heated political contest over the direction of the country ahead of the 2027 elections.

Ruto and his administration have faced criticism from opposition figures over the economy, cost of living and the government's record since taking office.

Gachagua's comments also followed his broader criticism of the government's economic record.

Earlier in the church address, he challenged Treasury Cabinet Secretary John Mbadi's argument that increased consumption of soft drinks could indicate improved household incomes.

Gachagua argued that ordinary Kenyans were experiencing economic difficulties despite government claims of improved economic indicators. He said declining church offerings would provide a more meaningful indication of household financial wellbeing.

“If you want to know if the economy is doing well, ask the pastor about the offering; it will tell you how the economy is moving,” he said.

He further urged Kenyans to prepare for political change in 2027, arguing that the country required new leadership.

“Let us get in line. We look for new leadership that will fix our country and return it to where Uhuru Kenyatta left us,” Gachagua said

World.title: LONDON HAS FALLEN
World.content:
I studied in London during 1970s amidst the IRA bombings – a time when the government encouraged you to conserve water and do joint showering.

It was a tough era and I remember walking almost daily from Queensway to Houghton Street to the London School of Economics in WC2 and back as the underground received bomb threats.

London has gone through many challenges from bombing during World War II plus before and after. Though it all, London survived and thrived.

Yet now I fear that London has truly fallen – and this time it was not due to an external enemy like Hitler or the IRA, but from within.

I was sitting at George, a club at Mount Street and enjoying a light lunch with Angela Forrester, a senior banker in the City and Keith Lavell, a prominent lawyer with a top global law firm.

Complaints about the mismanagement of London did not stop during our meal. I was having a cold Caesar salad, Angela a pasta and Keith a cod.

Angela was explaining how the Treasury and government policy has caused all the global investors and business leaders that lived in London to depart to Monaco, the Gulf and Italy.

She added as she was scooping her last spoonful of pasta that after the war in the gulf, Monaco and especially Milan were now the favorites for global business leaders.

Keith was criticizing Britain’s tax system, its exit from the EU, the high VAT and the unscrupulous bureaucracy.

As Keith put his knife and fork together signaling he had finished eating, he added that it was ridiculous that a UK citizen would, after paying tax all their life properly, have their heirs confronted by a 40 percent death tax.

This practice had families sell assets to pay this unwarranted tax.

I asked Keith, having finished my salad, about the fact that a UK resident with no UK income having their assets in a bonded warehouse in London would have their heirs confronted by the death tax.

How did that make sense?

Keith raised both his arms in the air explaining that irrationality is reigning and bringing the UK to its knees with the economy tanking.

Angela interrupted, saying she did not understand why VAT reimbursement has been cancelled for visitors and tourists causing them to buy elsewhere.

She added all of Europe reimburses VAT to foreigners as they exit from the EU and sadly London, who has the biggest number of tourists, does not do that, causing shops to close as buyers now buy from Paris, Rome, etc.

Any visitor to London sees multiple shops closed and with “for lease” signs on major London streets such as Regent’s Street, Oxford Street and Jermyn Street.

As we all got our plates removed, I asked, “What is the logic of the city of London having long term road closures for works that maximum would take a week, roads being narrowed with pavements being widened causing horrible traffic constriction?”

“Moreover.” I added “the uncomprehending fact of the “coning” of London.”

“Coning?” asked Angela with a puzzled look on her face as she pushed her blonde hair backwards.

“Yes,” I added. “You have these traffic cones everywhere, dividing tunnels and highways, and choking transport even when there is no work being done.”

I explained this phenomenon is destructive in so many ways, including but not limited to significant unnecessary delays and frustrations.

Angela agreed, explaining that several individuals missed their flights due to such traffic jams going to Heathrow, Stansted, Luton and Gatwick.

We all ordered coffee, two espressos for Angela and I whilst Keith ordered an americano.

Looking out the large window at George, rain started coming down in bucketfuls and people were rushing into shops.

The good news, as I returned to the conversation between Keith and Angela, was that such downpours lasted a brief period.

As the coffee arrived, Keith brought up the trains.

He had just returned from a business trip to Osaka and could not stop comparing the two systems. “In Japan,” he said, “if a train is four minutes late, the conductor issues a written apology. Here, we’ve normalized delays of forty minutes as if it’s weather.”

He said the average commuter into Waterloo or Victoria now builds in a buffer of twenty to thirty minutes just to account for “signal failures” that seem to occur with suspicious regularity.

Angela agreed, adding that she had missed a connecting flight at Heathrow last month because her domestic train from Manchester was cancelled without notice, and there had been no staff at the counter to explain why.

That led naturally into the topic of flights.

Angela said she now avoids British carriers when she has any onward connection that matters, because delays out of Heathrow and Gatwick have become so routine that colleagues in Frankfurt and Zurich joke about it openly in meetings.

“Nobody schedules a same-day connection through London anymore,” she said. “You build in a night in a hotel, just in case.”

As both Angela and Keith were exchanging poor experiences at London airports and flights, my mind soared to the earlier days when London was a leading and dominant city across the world.

I remember how when London city spoke, everyone listened, and how the audience arrived at the great London theaters in suits and cocktail dresses and not in flip flops and shorts as they do now.

How the audience respected the actors and made no noise, how London was the voice of creativity, discipline and diplomacy in the EU. I expected the UK to lead the EU rather than the chaotic Brexit vote and complexity of policies that followed and still occurs.

Before I returned to focus on the conversation at the table, my last thought was of Margaret Thatcher (1979-1990), John Major (1990-1997) and Tony Blair (1997-2007), all Prime Ministers with serious tenures and stability plus success regardless of some failed decisions

Since then, 10 Downing Street has become a revolving door, rivaling a period in Italy in the 1970s and 1980s when Prime Ministers rotated every two to three years with no policy nor success.

Angela pushed back gently, saying she did not want the lunch to end on such a grim note. She said London still has the ingredients – the institutions, the talent, the history – and that what’s missing is simply the vision, execution and discipline to use them.

I wanted to believe her. But walking out of George onto Mount Street, past a line of traffic cones sealing off a stretch of pavement where no workman had been seen in weeks, I found myself thinking about the other two times this city was meant to fall. In the Blitz, the enemy was visible, and so was the courage.

During the IRA years, we walked to school past bomb threats because the alternative was letting fear win.

Both times, London knew exactly what it was fighting and fought back.

This time there is no enemy to rally against, no siren to signal that the danger is here. Just a huge blindness – a tax system that punishes success, a bureaucracy that closes shops instead of opening them, a transport network that cannot keep a schedule, a government that changes its mind every two years.

London did not fall to an invasion. It is falling to its own inability to get out of its own way.

Keith caught up with me at the corner, still muttering about the cones.

“You know what the difference is,” he said, “That a recognized enemy can be defeated. I’m not sure we recognize that “coning” is an enemy.”

I didn’t have an answer for him. I still don’t. But I know this: a city that survived Hitler and survived the IRA should not be brought to its knees by roadworks that never finish, trains that never arrive, and a Treasury that cannot tell the difference between taxing wealth and driving it away.

London has fallen before, in ways far more literal.

What’s different now is that no one is quite sure who to blame, and no one in charge seems especially in a hurry to fix it.
